signals.title: [ACTP] orchestrate par-control tasks
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the production `par-control` orchestration loop. It dequeues tasks with bounded concurrency, starts the executor on demand, synchronizes signing keys, dispatches actions, and publishes outcomes. Executor idle shutdown is self-owned by the Go executor rather than driven by `par-control` process-manager calls. Task heartbeats run from dequeue through cold start, execution, and terminal publication. Runner health checks are independent of task flow, and shutdown drains in-flight work without calling `dd-procmgrd` from the shutdown path. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy --manifest-path pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 7 of 9; based on #54592 and followed by #54594._

This preserves the invariant that exactly one runner polls OPMS without disabling the only available runner. ### Validation - `bazel test //comp/privateactionrunner/impl:impl_test` Tests cover Linux and Windows hosts, containers, and unsupported platforms. _Stack 8 of 9; based on #54593 and followed by #54529._

signals.title: [CWS] fix matching sub-expression reporting in the And/Or operators
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes three defects in the way `And` and `Or` record matching sub-expressions in `pkg/security/secl/compiler/eval/operators.go`. One commit per fix, each with a test that fails before the corresponding change: 1. **Report evaluated values, not evaluator closures.** `Or` and `StringEquals` passed the operand's `EvalFnc` to `AddMatchingSubExpr` instead of the value it returned, so `MatchingValue.Value` held a `func(*Context) T` rather than the matched bool/string. 2. **Stop re-evaluating `And` operands.** The three dynamic branches of `And` invoked their operand evaluators a second time purely to fill in `MatchingValue.Value`, so every reported operand was evaluated twice on a match. 3. **Keep the reported field paired with its operand across the weight swap.** `And`/`Or` reorder their operands so the cheaper one runs first, but only the evaluators were swapped — the `Field` and `Offset` used for reporting kept the original order. ### Motivation (1) is user-visible. `newRuleContext` in `pkg/security/serializers/serializers_base.go` runs the reported value through a type switch whose `default` branch does `fmt.Sprintf("%v", value)`; a func lands there, so the event payload carried a pointer address instead of the matched value. (2) is on the hot path. Operands can be patterns, regexps or iterators (weights up to 2000 in `eval.go`), so this doubled their cost on every match, and it silently assumed the evaluators were side-effect free. (3) makes `Or` attribute a match to the operand that did not match, highlighting the wrong span of the rule expression. It only triggers when the weights are such that a swap happens. `And` was not observably affected, since both operands are true whenever it reports, but it is reordered the same way and is updated for consistency. The generated operators in `eval_operators.go` and their template in `pkg/security/generators/operators` were checked and are already correct — all four sites were in the hand-written `operators.go`. ### Describe how you validated your changes Three new tests in `compiler/eval/eval_test.go`, each verified to fail against the unfixed operator and pass after: - `TestMatchingSubExprReportedValues` — asserts the reported values are the evaluated ones and rejects any `reflect.Func`. Fails on `false || process.is_root` and `true && process.name == process.name`. - `TestMatchingSubExprSingleEvaluation` — counts evaluations of `process.is_root` through a new `isRootEvalCount` counter on the test model (alongside the existing `uidEvaluated`/`gidEvaluated`). Fails on all four affected `And` branches. - `TestMatchingSubExprOperandSwap` — builds the operands by hand, because the test model has no boolean field carrying a weight, so the reordering cannot be triggered from a SECL expression. Covers both swap directions plus a no-swap regression guard. The existing `TestMatchingSubExprs` and the full `pkg/security/secl` suite pass; `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean. ### Additional Notes No release note: none of these change documented behavior, and the payload defect in (1) was emitting a pointer address where a value was expected.
signals.author: paulcacheux

signals.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded two independent ways: 1. **Flag allowlist** — the kernel only reports flags intersecting `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. `CLONE_NEWCGROUP` is excluded per the requester's note on CWS-6628 (it only moves the caller into the current cgroup namespace), as are the non-namespace flags. 2. **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of either gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. The `flags` field always carries the **full raw bitmask**, so rules can inspect any flag — including ones outside the allowlist — once an event fires. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: fix(e2e): retry ensure-adws-started on transient SSH/script failures
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds an onError resource hook that retries the ensure-adws-started command when sshd dies mid-command or the command's own PowerShell errors out, without retrying dial-exhaustion failures or the whole stack up. ### Motivation ensure-adws-started fails flakily shortly after domain-controller promotion (WINA-2095) due to transient SSH/script issues that a retry fixes. Requires the CI Pulumi CLI/engine to be bumped to >= v3.219.0 for onError hook support (tracked separately). ### Describe how you validated your changes Windows e2e tests should pass.
signals.author: clarkb7

signals.title: [SBOM] Skip images whose SBOM cannot be uncompressed
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? processImageSBOM logged the error from UncompressSBOM and carried on, but UncompressSBOM returns no SBOM alongside its error, so reading its status a few lines later dereferenced a nil pointer. The check worker recovers from a panic in Run, so that one misbehaving check cannot take the process with it, but the long-running check wrapper returns from Run as soon as it has started the goroutine the check really runs on, and the recover never covers that goroutine. An image whose stored SBOM cannot be uncompressed therefore brings the whole Agent down, and does so again at every refresh for as long as workloadmeta holds it. Skip the image instead. It is reported again once it is scanned anew.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: [SBOM] Refresh every image when spreading the refresh
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? The spread refresher divides the image count by the number of steps it spreads a period over to decide how many images to refresh per step. The division truncates, so a host with fewer than ten images refreshed none of them, ever. An image SBOM was then sent only when the image changed or when a container first ran it, so inUse stayed true after the last container stopped. Above ten, unless the count was a multiple of ten, the refresh was merely slower than configured. Fifteen images took one and a half periods to cycle. Round the count up. Every image is then covered within one period, at the cost of at most nine extra refreshes per period. That overhead only matters where images are few, and a host with a single image now sends it once per step rather than once per period. The refresher is off by default, so this only affects hosts that set sbom.container_image.use_spread_refresher.

signals.title: [procmgr] Windows spawn profiles foundation
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Introduces **Windows spawn profiles** in dd-procmgr so managed children can run under different security contexts: - **Privileged**: spawn as LocalSystem (supervisor primary token) - **AgentUser**: spawn as the agent service account (`ddagentuser`) Adds the Windows spawn stack (token logon, user profile load, supervision job, suspended `CreateProcessAsUserW`), a **privileged spawn catalog** that rejects unexpected command/args/env for privileged children, and **gRPC named-pipe caller authentication** for mutating RPCs. Also refactors the daemon runtime into a **`Supervisor` event loop** plus `ProcessManager` handlers, and runs **dd-procmgr-service as LocalSystem** so agent-profile spawn can read the agent password from LSA. **Stack context (PR 1):** | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | This PR | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on this PR; not on the merge spine) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | **Explicitly deferred:** config gates (#54732), secret-backend cache invalidation (#54734), process-agent dual-mode (#54735), full `ReloadConfig` (#55080). RPC/CLI for reload stay in this PR but return `UNIMPLEMENTED` until #55080. ### Motivation Process-agent on Windows must run as LocalSystem; other agent children should stay on the agent user. Spawn profiles make that explicit and enforceable at spawn time, and are a prerequisite for moving process-agent supervision off legacy SCM in #54735. LocalSystem MSI lands here so agent-profile children (ADP, PAR, DDOT) can spawn without waiting for #54735. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Bazel/Cargo procmgr Rust unit tests (Linux + Windows CI) - Privileged spawn catalog and spawn-profile unit tests (`pkg/procmgr/rust/...`) - COAT package tests (`pkg/procmgr/coat/...`) - Windows new-e2e: ADP, PAR, DDOT running tests, plus LocalSystem / agent-user identity checks (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-runtimes/procmgr/`) ### Additional Notes - **Fleet:** DDOT extension uninstall uses `ReloadOrRestartProcmgr()` (reload stub → SCM restart fallback). No process-agent dual-mode changes in this PR. - **ReloadConfig:** Proto and `dd-procmgr reload` remain for API compatibility; handler returns `UNIMPLEMENTED` until [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). - Supersedes the spawn portion of [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249).
signals.author: jose-manuel-almaza

signals.title: [procmgr] Config gates for processes.d auto-start
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds **config gates** to dd-procmgr so `processes.d` definitions can use `condition_config_any` to auto-start only when Agent config says they should. Implementation mirrors the Windows legacy SCM startup checks in `dependent_services_windows.go` and Agent config resolution: - YAML lookup (case-insensitive keys, flattened dotted keys, permissive parse fallback, merge keys) - Environment bindings (`DD_*`) with Agent precedence (ignore empty values, no trim before `ParseBool`, legacy `process_config.enabled` transforms) - Fleet policy merge - Derived `system_probe_config.enabled` (USM/NPM/security knobs, sk-tracer and discovery adjustments) - Windows: read `DD_*` overrides from the core Agent SCM `Environment` registry when not set in the procmgr process env Wires gate evaluation into `ManagedProcess` start/reload paths in the manager. **Stack context:** PR 2. Builds on [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) (`jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles`). List/describe (#53568) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | This PR | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation Moving subservices (starting with process-agent) to dd-procmgr requires the supervisor to apply the same start/stop rules as the Agent today. Without config gates, a `processes.d` entry would always spawn when registered, which breaks parity with legacy SCM and fleet policy. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/` (env bindings, YAML load, system-probe derivations, gate evaluation) - Go unit tests for Windows config helpers (`pkg/config/setup/config_windows_test.go`) - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI ### Additional Notes - No `ENC[...]` / secret backend resolution in this PR (fleet policy `ENC[...]` values are not resolved here either). - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Schema comment sync in `pkg/config/schema/yaml/process_config.yaml` for env binding documentation. - Small exports in `pkg/system-probe/config/` so procmgr gate derivations stay aligned with Go `adjust*` logic.
signals.author: jose-manuel-almaza

signals.title: [procmgr] Secret backend resolution for config gates
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Resolves `ENC[...]` values during config gate evaluation so dd-procmgr matches Agent secret handling. Adds: - `config_gate/secrets.rs`: resolve handles via `secret_backend_command`, native `secret_backend_type`, and `multi_secret_backends` (same precedence as the core Agent) - Platform secret backend runners (Windows `CreateProcessAsUserW` under the Agent account; Unix setuid when procmgr runs as root for Privileged children) - `secret_backend_exec.rs`: shared spawn, timeout, stdout drain, and response parsing - Windows ACL validation on secret backend executables before spawn - Agent config precedence for backend settings: `DD_SECRET_BACKEND_*` env (including core Agent SCM `Environment` on Windows) over `datadog.yaml` - Manager reload: invalidate secret caches when config changes Fleet policy `ENC[...]` values stay unresolved here, matching Agent `MergeFleetPolicy` running after secret resolution. **Stack context:** PR 3. Builds on [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) (`jose/procmgr-config-gates`). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | This PR | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation PR 2 config gates read YAML, env, and fleet policy, but many customers gate features with secret-backed settings (`ENC[api_key]`, secret-backed booleans, etc.). Without secret resolution, gates would mis-evaluate and auto-start behavior would diverge from the Agent. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/secrets.rs` and config gate integration tests (serialized env to avoid cross-test leakage) - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI - Linux CI: secret-backend tests run under the agent service user where required ### Additional Notes - Secret backends always run as the core Agent service account, not as the procmgr supervisor (LocalSystem) or a Privileged managed child. - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Invokes `secret-generic-connector` when no custom `secret_backend_command` is configured.

signals.title: [procmgr] Supervise process-agent on Windows via dd-procmgr
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Moves Windows **process-agent** supervision to **dd-procmgr** using the same dual-mode pattern as PAR: - Fleet installer writes `processes.d/datadog-agent-process.yaml` (Privileged spawn profile) - Legacy `datadog-process-agent` SCM service is suppressed when procmgr owns process-agent - Agent startup waits on `dd-procmgr-service` before starting gated legacy children; independent services (sysprobe, security-agent, installer) start without blocking on procmgr **Stack context:** PR 4. Builds on [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) → [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) → [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). List/describe (#53568) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. Reload lands in [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | This PR | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation We want subservices on dd-procmgr instead of SCM. Process-agent needs LocalSystem on Windows; other agent children should stay on the agent user. This PR wires the product integration once the procmgr foundation (PRs 1–3) is in place. `dd-procmgr-service` already runs as LocalSystem from [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). ### Describe how you validated your changes - Go unit tests for dependent Windows service startup (`dependent_services_windows_test.go`) - Go unit tests for fleet installer templates and YAML path substitution (`processmanager/...`) - New Windows E2E: process-agent supervised by procmgr, runs as LocalSystem, legacy SCM stopped ### Additional Notes - Linux process-agent stays on systemd for now. Legacy SCM service registration is not removed yet. - Process-agent `processes.d` config uses the shared `install_root` helper (same as PAR/ADP). MSI `RemoveFolderEx` handles uninstall/rollback cleanup; no per-file MSI rollback custom actions. - Includes release note `windows-process-procmgr-dual-mode-b7d2e4a1c8f03962.yaml`. - Closes/supersedes [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249) once the full stack merges.

signals.title: remove unneeded python spec in legacy omnibus
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Remove unneeded python spec in legcay omnibus - Lift python3.rb dependency up datadog-agent-integrations-py3 - Add the missing license declaration for //deps:cpython - put all the files for cpython together in deps/cpython. This preserves the license we were using before. It also preserves the fact that the Omnibus build was using a personal copy cached at https://dd-agent-omnibus.s3.amazonaws.com/licenses/Python-2.0. That's not great - we should use the upstream license, but the upstream license is not a true copy of the license. It has history which is unrelated to the current license, so it is actually less good than our copy. This is a thing to sort out in the future. At least now the fact that we use a private copy is explicit, rather than being hidden in the omnibus code. ### Motivation - Do not specify the python version in two places, while only using it in one. Every time integrations updated python, they would needlessly update the omnibus scripts and cpython.MODULE.bazel - Remove dead code. All omnibus scripting is going away. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI - The missing file detector does not show that we lost the license. Early runs did, so I have confidence that CI correctly detects it. - The missing file detector says the license file is slightly renamed. The content is the same. The renaming is a legally allowed transformation. What matters is that we have the content of the license in the distribution, not what we name it.

signals.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signals.title: [CWS] Fix: handle activity dump endpoint host that already embeds a port
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes CWS activity dump uploads to dual-shipped `additional_endpoints` whose `host` already includes a port (e.g. `cws-intake.datadoghq.com.:443`). `GetEndpointURL` was appending the port a second time, producing a malformed `[host:port]:port` authority that failed URL parsing — so every upload to that endpoint failed with an `invalid port` error. The host is now split before joining, so an embedded port is honored instead of duplicated. An explicitly configured port still wins, and bare IPv6 literals are untouched. ### Motivation In prod, CWS activity dumps were failing to reach the secondary (dual-ship) endpoint.
signals.author: kovagsm

signals.title: [NETPATH-1108] Remove flaky RC re-poll gate from Dynamic Path e2e test Setup
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes the synchronization in `TestHostTrafficDynamicPathSuite` without relying on fakeintake's global Remote Config poll counter. - Adds the `NETWORK_PATH` Remote Config document immediately after `BaseSuite.SetupSuite`, before curl, DNS, and resolver setup. - Removes both `RCStats().Polls` gates. - Keeps the traffic generator running for 6 minutes so it outlives the test's 5-minute eventual assertion. JIRA: [NETPATH-1108](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/NETPATH-1108) ### Motivation The suite has intermittently failed on `main` in `SetupSuite` with: > `agent did not poll Remote Config after the dynamic config was added` The E2E framework configures the Agent to poll fakeintake every 5 seconds, so the production default 1-minute cadence was not the cause. The flake came from the interaction between the test's setup order and fakeintake's empty Remote Config behavior: 1. The suite performed package, DNS, and resolver setup before adding its first `NETWORK_PATH` config. 2. During that time, the Agent polled fakeintake's empty RC repository. 3. Fakeintake records those requests in `RCStats().Polls` but returns HTTP 404 when no requested product has a config. 4. Those responses increased the Agent's exponential retry backoff, so the next poll could fall outside the setup gate's 2-minute deadline. The poll counter was also not a reliable synchronization signal: it increments before fakeintake knows whether the request can be served and therefore does not prove that this config was fetched or applied. Taking the counter baseline after `RCAddConfig` also allowed a successful fetch between those two calls to be missed, forcing the test to wait for an unnecessary additional poll. The test's existing payload assertion is the stronger end-to-end proof. Local configuration excludes all destinations, and the expected Network Path event must contain the exact remote `test_config_id`, `test_config_source`, and tags. Observing that event proves the config was fetched, applied by the deployed Agent, exercised by matching host traffic, and forwarded to fakeintake. Adding the config first minimizes empty-repository polling during setup. Keeping traffic active beyond the full assertion window ensures a delayed RC application still receives matching connections to admit. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `git diff --check` - Confirmed the existing `new-e2e-netpath` CI job covers `./tests/netpath`. - Local live E2E was intentionally skipped; `new-e2e-netpath` will exercise the change in CI. No production code is changed. [NETPATH-1108]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/NETPATH-1108?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: Sign macos DMG only on nightly instead of main
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Stops doing real signing and notarization of Macos DMG packages on main. Do it on nightly only so we maintain some testing of the process. ### Motivation We should not be creating notarized, installable packages off of main. That creates artifacts which could appear to be end-user consumable, but are not supported, nor necessarily validated. Notarization also slightly DOSes Apple. Ideally we should only do notarization on the release branches for candidate builds. We'll address that once we convert the build to bazel. ### Describe how you validated your changes CI ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [APM] Reduce allocations on the trace decode path
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Two independent allocation reductions on the trace-agent receive/decode path. **1. Intern strings directly from the payload (v0.4 decode).** `parseStringBytesRef` materialized a Go string for every value just to look it up in the payload's string table, discarding it on a hit. **2. Reserve `bytes.MinRead` beyond the body when buffering a request.** `reserveBodySize` reserved exactly `Content-Length`, but `io.Copy` bottoms out in `bytes.Buffer.ReadFrom`, which needs `bytes.MinRead` of spare capacity for the read that reports EOF. Also fixes two swapped godoc names on `parseStringBytes` / `parseStringBytesRef`. ### Motivation Both were found in a staging heap profile of the trace-agent receiver. `pprof -traces` showed `bytes.Buffer.Grow` and `bytes.Buffer.ReadFrom` both allocating on the same `copyRequestBody` path — i.e. twice per request. ### Describe how you validated your changes New tests and benchmarks in both packages: - `pkg/proto/pbgo/trace/idx/string_intern_test.go` — `TestAddBytesMatchesAdd` asserts `AddBytes` and `Add` are behaviourally equivalent, so no decode divergence is introduced. - `pkg/proto/pbgo/trace/idx/string_intern_bench_test.go` — intern benchmarks across hit rates, including a `HitRate0` control arm. - `pkg/trace/api/body_buffer_test.go` — `TestReserveBodySizeLimit` pins the `MaxRequestBytes` boundary (at / one over / absent / unparseable), confirming the `MinRead` padding does not leak into the size check. `TestCopyRequestBodyNoRealloc` asserts the body lands in the same backing array that was reserved, by identity, rather than counting allocations. - `pkg/trace/api/body_buffer_bench_test.go` — `BenchmarkCopyRequestBody` over two regimes: `SmallWarmPool` (ordinary traffic, shows the change is neutral, 0 allocs/op) and `LargeColdBuffer` (the regime that actually generates the bytes). Also run: full `pkg/trace/api` and `pkg/proto/pbgo/trace/idx` suites, and `bazel test //pkg/proto/pbgo/trace/idx:idx_test //pkg/trace/api:api_test` — all pass. **Time** (benchstat, n=10, Apple M4 Max darwin/arm64; only `span.go` differs between arms) | Benchmark | before | after | delta | |---|---|---|---| | `StringTableIntern/HitRate100` | 24.42µ ± 4% | 14.74µ ± 1% | −39.6% | | `StringTableIntern/HitRate90` | 27.90µ ± 3% | 18.90µ ± 1% | −32.3% | | `StringTableIntern/HitRate50` | 31.80µ ± 2% | 25.63µ ± 1% | −19.4% | | `StringTableIntern/HitRate0` | 35.32µ ± 5% | 34.40µ ± 0% | −2.6% | | `SpanUnmarshalConvertedStrings` | 107.80µ ± 1% | 86.15µ ± 1% | −20.1% | **Allocations** | Benchmark | before | after | delta | |---|---|---|---| | `HitRate100` | 1003 allocs / 48288 B | 4 allocs / 336 B | −99.6% / −99.3% | | `HitRate90` | 1005 allocs / 44.3KiB | 105 allocs / 9.1KiB | −89.6% / −79.4% | | `HitRate50` | 1005 allocs / 73.8KiB | 505 allocs / 54.2KiB | −49.8% / −26.5% | | `HitRate0` | 1007 allocs / 108.4KiB | 1007 allocs / 108.4KiB | ~ (identical) | | `SpanUnmarshalConvertedStrings` | 3607 allocs / 227.6KiB | 1231 allocs / 197.9KiB | −65.9% / −13.1% | **Throughput on the end-to-end span decode: 417.5 → 522.4 MiB/s, +25.1%.** ### Additional Notes

signals.title: fix(installer): embed -nocap systemd unit templates
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds `//go:embed` directives for `tmpl/gen/oci-nocap/*.service` and `tmpl/gen/debrpm-nocap/*.service`, and the matching Bazel `embedsrcs` entries, so the `-nocap` systemd unit templates ship inside the installer binary. Adds `embed_test.go`, which enumerates units through the `embed.FS` and asserts `GetSystemdUnit` resolves every unit in both the ambient-capability and `-nocap` variants. ## Motivation This is to address this escalation: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/AGENT-16750 `GetSystemdUnit` selects the `-nocap` templates on hosts whose kernel does not support ambient capabilities (older than 4.3), but no `//go:embed` directive covered those directories. Unit generation failed at runtime with: ``` failed to write stable units: open tmpl/gen/debrpm-nocap/datadog-agent.service: file does not exist ``` The package manager scriptlet ignores that failure, so the install reported success while the host was left with no Datadog units and `systemctl start datadog-agent` returned `Unit not found`. Both the classic DEB/RPM path and Fleet Automation remote upgrades and config experiments (`oci-nocap`) were affected. The existing tests missed this because they read the template tree from disk instead of from the `embed.FS`, so the templates were always present regardless of the embed directives. ## Verification - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded` - 83 tests passed - `bazel test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded:all` - `embedded_test` and `tmpl_test` passed - The new `TestGetSystemdUnitEmbedsAllVariants` fails on `main` (`file does not exist` for every `-nocap` unit) and passes with this change - `TestGetSystemdUnitSelectsNocapVariant` confirms the `-nocap` unit actually has `AmbientCapabilities=` stripped, not just that it loads ### Known gap, not addressed here `tmpl/datadog-agent-data-plane.service.tmpl` emits `AmbientCapabilities` unconditionally, without the `{{ if .AmbiantCapabilitiesSupported }}` guard its siblings use, so its two variants are byte-identical. That is a pre-existing template defect, out of scope for this fix, and is documented in a comment on the test. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: feat(notableevents): add macOS shutdown-cause notable event
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a macOS notable event that reports **why the previous boot ended**, recovered after the fact from the PMU rather than observed live. On Apple silicon, PMU/PMIC driver services publish an `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` IORegistry property: an array of short ASCII tokens naming the fault conditions that preceded the last power-off. This PR reads that property, classifies the tokens, and emits one notable event per boot when the classification is a fault. Five fault classes are covered, spanning the whole dictionary of 80 known tokens — 59 of which are faults: | Class | Title | Tokens | Example families | | ---------- | ------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------- | | `thermal` | macOS overheated shutdown | 14 | `ot`, `sochot`, `ntc_shdn` | | `power` | macOS power fault shutdown | 29 | `uv`, `ov`, `oc`, `buck`, `pgood` | | `crash` | macOS crash shutdown | 6 | `crash` | | `watchdog` | macOS watchdog timeout shutdown | 5 | `timeout` | | `hardware` | macOS hardware fault shutdown | 5 | `spmi`, `sgpio`, `fault`, `otp_crc` | - **Native reader** (`shutdown_cause_iokit_darwin.{c,h}`) walks the IOService plane, flattens every `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` array into a single `0x1f`-separated token sequence, and dedups as it writes — so no Core Foundation type crosses the cgo boundary. The whole plane is walked rather than matching a class because the publishing class is PMIC-specific and varies by Mac model, and IOKit cannot match on a property key alone (`kIOPropertyMatchKey` matches key *and* value). - **Classifier** (`shutdown_classify_darwin.go`) maps a token to its *family* (prefix before the first comma, a declared underscore family, or the whole token) and the family to one of five classes, resolved by fixed precedence: **thermal → power → crash → watchdog → hardware**. Thermal wins deliberately: a machine collapsing from heat also asserts reset, crash and power lines, and the event that matters most must not be titled as a crash. - **Event shape** (`format_darwin.go`) — `EventType` is the constant `"System shutdown fault"` so consumers can filter shutdown causes on one value; the class varies the title and message only. The payload reports every token observed *plus* the families and the fault subset the classifier acted on, so a reader sees both the raw evidence and what the verdict was based on: ```json "macos_shutdown_cause": { "source": "IOPMUBootFaultInfo", "classification": "thermal", "primary_family": "ot", "families": ["ot", "sochot"], "tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "fault_tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "boot_uuid": "…", "boot_time": "2026-08-11T09:55:21Z" } ``` - **Dedup is boot-scoped.** Identity is `shutdown:<bootUUID>:<sortedFaultTokens>`, hashed under a new `macos-shutdown-v1:` event-ID prefix. Both halves are load-bearing: the boot UUID alone says nothing about *what* was read, and the token set alone is identical across boots — a Mac that overheats every afternoon would emit one ID forever and be deduplicated into silence. Tokens are sorted first because PMU enumeration order is not stable (measured: two triggers with an identical fault set reported the groups in different order). - **Storage.** A new `ShutdownCause` bookmark field records the examined boot *whether or not* an event was emitted, so a cleanly-rebooting Mac does not re-read the property on every Agent restart. It is the primary guard rather than the `Acknowledged` map, which prunes after 30 days or 4096 entries — a Mac up longer than that would otherwise re-emit. The check runs **once per collector lifetime**, before the first directory scan, and is retried from the reconcile tick when it could not commit. It reads the property as an ordinary user (no root needed; system-probe runs as root regardless), and the whole feature is gated behind the existing `notable_events.enabled` setting, which defaults to `false`. **No benchmarks, deliberately.** There is no steady-state cost to measure: the IOService walk happens once per collector lifetime, is bounded at 16 services, and short-circuits as soon as every distinct token is accounted for. It is not on any per-event, per-scan or per-tick path. **Bookmark schema version stays at 1, deliberately.** `Load()` and `validateDarwinBookmarkState()` both require exact equality, so bumping to `2` would fail every existing v1 bookmark as corrupt — which resets state and re-baselines, discarding pending undelivered crash events on every upgraded host. `ShutdownCause` is `omitempty` with a nil zero value, so v1 bookmarks deserialize with no migration. Relatedly, `types.IsEventID()` had to learn the new prefix in the same change: a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID written under the old single-prefix check would fail validation on the next `Load()` and wipe the bookmark, silently losing every pending crash event. ### Motivation [https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040) **A hard shutdown kills the Agent before it can report why.** Whether the machine overheated, lost a power rail, asserted its CRASH line, tripped a watchdog or hit a hardware fault, the Agent is gone before it can say so — the cause has to be recovered from the PMU on the next boot, or it is never recovered at all. All five fault classes are in scope here; thermal is one of them, not the point of the feature. **Predecessor: macOS app crash notable events (#54084).** This builds directly on it, reusing its bookmark, its `Pending`/`Ack` delivery contract and its at-least-once semantics unchanged — a second event *source* on that pipeline, not a second pipeline. It complements rather than replaces it: #54084 reports `.ips` files, which are written by a *running* OS about a *running* process, so a PMU-forced power cut leaves no `.ips` at all. The one adjacent artifact that does exist, `.shutdownStall` spindumps, records a *stalled* shutdown, not its cause. Everything else was surveyed and rejected: `pmset -g log` carries no cause data (25,117 lines grepped, nothing), `nvram -p` has no shutdown-cause variable, `ioreg -rc IOPMrootDomain` has no such property, `last -x reboot` is empty, and the `AppleSMC: Previous shutdown cause: <N>` unified-log line that Intel Macs emit **does not exist on Apple silicon**. Without this, a machine that overheated or lost a power rail badly enough to be cut off is a silent gap in the fleet record. `kern.shutdownreason` is **deliberately not read** — not as a source, not as a fallback, not as payload. It is the same PMU data flattened into an 80-byte-capped string, and it was already destroying data on an ordinary clean shutdown of the test machine: the cap was hit in 4 of 6 measured boots, always cutting *mid-token* and synthesising fault names that do not exist (`crash,crash`, `btn_rst,btn`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_d`). Absence of a token from that sysctl carries no information at all. The tradeoff is accepted and known: the sysctl also carries application-processor tokens (`ap_restart`, `ap_panic`) that `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not, and this PR gives those up rather than add a second parsing path and a second failure mode. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests — 240 tests pass in `pkg/notableevents`** (verified locally on the branch head with `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/notableevents/...`). Classifier tests deliberately use **payloads measured from real hardware** as fixtures rather than invented ones: | Pattern | Tokens (distinct union) | Emits | | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | A — clean shutdown | `target_off_restart`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | B — `sudo reboot` | `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | C — button/force restart | + `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `crash,crash0_in` | `crash`, `fault_tokens = ["crash,crash0_in"]` | Also covered: the full 80-token dictionary maps to exactly one family each with the asserted **59 fault / 21 benign** split (14 thermal, 29 power, 6 crash, 5 watchdog, 5 hardware) — this pins a typo in the family map that would otherwise silently misclassify; class precedence in every pairing; unknown *suffix* within a known family (`ot,some_future_sensor`) still classifies thermal, which is the prefix contract; permuted group order yields an identical event ID; benign-token exclusions are dead-weight-free (each is in the measured dictionary *and* would otherwise be a fault); every classification fits the wire limit; malformed and oversized payloads are rejected. Collector tests cover the delivery contract end to end: one event per boot; `Start()` → `Close()` → `Start()` yields one event, not two; same boot UUID after Ack yields nothing; a *different* boot UUID with the same tokens yields a new event; a saturated pending queue **defers** rather than records, because recording the boot would be final and the fault cannot be reproduced by a later boot; a `Save` failure leaves nothing pending and is retried; a check blocked by an in-flight bookmark commit is retried from the reconcile tick rather than stranded for the process lifetime; reader failure, absent property and untrusted payload all leave crash-report collection unaffected; a v1 bookmark with no `shutdown_cause` key loads without being treated as corrupt. **Manual QA on real hardware.** `Mac17,9` / M5 Pro / macOS 26.5.2 (`25F84`), SIP enabled, no `boot-args`. **Six real boot sessions** executed one trigger at a time — the property is destroyed by the next reboot, so the runs could not be batched — with an immediate capture script per boot: `sudo reboot`, Control-Command-Power force restart, power button held ~10s, a deliberately stalled shutdown ended by the power button, the same stall resolved via Try Again → Force Quit, and a battery run-down. Three distinct payloads were observed across six distinct boot UUIDs, verified byte-identical by MD5, reverting to pattern A after a clean shutdown. That establishes the load-bearing premise: **the property is a live, event-driven, self-clearing signal, not a constant** — which is what validates both the read path and the boot-UUID dedup key. **How to reproduce a fault event yourself — the `crash` class, on demand.** One fault class is reproducible at will on Apple silicon, so a reviewer can exercise the whole path end to end without waiting for real hardware trouble. A force restart asserts the AP's CRASH line, which emits `crash,crash0_in`: 1. Enable the feature — it is off by default: ```bash # datadog.yaml notable_events: enabled: true ``` 2. Clear any prior bookmark so the check is not skipped as already-examined, and note that the file is root-owned: ```bash sudo rm -f /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json ``` 3. Record the current boot identity and the pre-restart payload, for comparison: ```bash sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo ``` 4. Force restart: hold **Control-Command-Power** until the screen blanks. (Holding the power button ~10s, or ending a stalled shutdown with the power button, both produce the same payload — see the resolution caveat in Additional Notes.) 5. After the machine boots, confirm the PMU now reports the crash token. Expect pattern C — `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `target_off_restart`, `crash,crash0_in`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert`: ```bash ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid # must differ from step 3 ``` 6. Start the Agent and system-probe, and confirm the event: ```bash sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.agent sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.sysprobe sudo cat /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json | jq . ``` Expect a `shutdown_cause` object whose `boot_uuid` matches step 5, and a `pending` entry with a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID, `"event_type": "System shutdown fault"`, title `macOS crash shutdown`, `"classification": "crash"`, and `fault_tokens` of exactly `["crash,crash0_in"]` — all six tokens appear in `tokens`, but only the crash one elected the class. 7. Confirm the dedup guard: restart the Agent without rebooting. No second event should be emitted, and `shutdown_cause.boot_uuid` should be unchanged. To verify the **negative** case, `sudo reboot` instead of step 4 (pattern B) or shut down cleanly from the Apple menu (pattern A). Both must produce a `shutdown_cause` record with **no** event — a clean shutdown emitting an event is the failure mode most worth catching, since `wdog,reset_in_1` is present on every ordinary shutdown. **`qa/rc-required` — why this needs RC validation.** The classes that matter most in the field cannot be triggered on any machine we control, and cannot be simulated at all: the property is written by the PMU at power-off and is read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store. Reproducing a genuine thermal, power-rail or hardware fault means real failing hardware. Virtualized macOS runners expose no PMU, so the property is simply absent there and CI can only assert graceful degradation. What RC deployment adds is a full end-to-end test on real hardware: that the notable event is actually emitted and delivered, and that its tags and payload arrive intact. The predecessor, #54084, carried the same label for the same reason. **What was NOT validated, and cannot be:** - **No thermal token has ever been observed on this machine** — not `ot,*`, not `sochot,*`, not `ntc_shdn`. The thermal classification is inferred from token names in the PMU's own declared dictionary (published as `info-fault_name-<N>` properties on the `pmu,spmi` device-tree nodes). This is a hard limit, not a gap in the testing: there is **no native way to fake a thermal shutdown cause**. The value is produced by the PMU at power-off and exposed read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store — `sysctl -w` refuses (read-only OID), there is no user-settable IORegistry path, no `nvram` variable, and a userspace `os_log` line would not carry the right sender image. Generating real heat was out of scope. **The thermal path should not be described as verified in any customer-facing text or release note.** - **The real IOKit read on CI.** macOS VMs expose no PMU, so the property is absent and the reader returns empty. No E2E test is added; on a virtualized runner one could only assert graceful degradation, which is worth having but would not be thermal coverage. ### Additional Notes **Known tradeoff — `crash` fires on user force-restarts.** Measured, not hypothetical: `crash,crash0_in` appeared in pattern C with no panic induced. The token means the AP's CRASH line was asserted, which a hard reset satisfies, so **every user-initiated force restart on this hardware emits a `crash`-classified event.** Accepted because a force restart is itself a signal that something went wrong badly enough that the user gave up on the machine, and the alternative — treating the family as benign — silently dropped genuine AP and hypervisor crashes. Two commitments follow: the message says "followed a CRASH signal from the processor" and never claims a kernel panic; and if force restarts dominate emitted volume, the fix is to split `crash,hyp_*` from `crash,crash*_in`, not to revert the family to benign. **Fault allowlist, not benign denylist.** Under a denylist, any Mac whose clean shutdown emits an uncatalogued token would raise a shutdown-fault event on *every boot*. A permanent false positive is noticed and distrusted; a missed rare fault is not. The cost is that a genuinely new fault token on unfamiliar hardware is dropped silently — mitigated by matching on the family *prefix*, so `ot,anything_new` still classifies thermal. **Two benign per-token exceptions** (`shutdownBenignTokens`), for tokens whose family is a fault but whose meaning is not: `buck_boot_charge` (booting after the battery charged from depleted, not a regulator failure) and `timeout,dblclick_timeout` (the power-button double-click window). Both produced a user-visible fault event on a machine that had not faulted. Scoped to these two deliberately — the other `buck_*` tokens name real regulator failures. Excluding one only changes the outcome when it is the sole evidence for its class. **Graceful degradation is strictly additive** — nothing here can block `Start()` or interfere with crash-report collection. Property absent → no event, debug log. IOKit failure → no event. `kern.bootsessionuuid` unreadable → skip the whole check, since without a dedup key an event could repeat on every Agent restart. `kern.boottime` unreadable → fall back to the current time and omit `boot_time`. Event over the wire limit → drop and warn, **never truncate a fault payload**, because a truncated one would be misleading. Save-failure and saturation warnings latch so a persistent condition warns once rather than on every reconcile tick, and are kept separate so neither can silence the other. **Bounds are derived from real hardware, and shared between C and Go so they cannot drift.** `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKENS_PER_SERVICE 88` and `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKEN_CHARS 53` come from the largest known real payload (80-token dictionary, longest token 35 bytes) plus margin — 10% on count, 50% on length — and the Go-side `maxShutdownTokens` / `maxShutdownTokenBytes` are derived from those same macros. `DD_PMU_MAX_SERVICES` is 16, matching how few PMU-publishing services exist in practice. A service exceeding its bounds is dropped and logged rather than failing the read; an oversized token is truncated rather than dropping its whole service; the walk stops early once every distinct token is accounted for, since no remaining service can contribute one that has not been seen. **Intel Macs silently emit nothing.** `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not exist there; `readPMUBootFaultInfo` returns `errShutdownCauseUnsupported` when `runtime.GOARCH != "arm64"`. The Intel path (SMC shutdown-cause code `-81` via `log show`, which needs root) is unimplemented and unvalidated — no Intel Mac available. Apple documents none of this property: `org:apple-oss-distributions` returns zero hits for both `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` and `info-fault_name`. Provenance is the device's own ADT table, community string dumps of the `AppleD2255PMU` kext, and independent confirmation of the prefix decodings in `hack-different/apple-knowledge`. The *read mechanism*, by contrast, is entirely public API: `IOServiceMatching`, `IOServiceGetMatchingServices`, `IOIteratorNext`, `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty`.

signals.title: [SVLS-9526] Prototype: serverless-init inventory payload + 9-platform POC deploy scripts
signals.text: ## What this is A **prototype branch** containing the full stack of changes for SVLS-9526 in a single PR. Intended for review and discussion — these changes will be broken into the stacked PRs below before merge. ## Stacked PRs (final form) | PR | Branch | Contents | |---|---|---| | #54537 | `svls-9526/force-collect` | `ForceCollect()` — send inventory payload on every cold start | | #54538 | `svls-9526/diagnostic-v2` | `inventories_first_run_delay` config key + diagnostic enhancements | | #54543 | `svls-9526/serverless-agent-table` | `cmd/serverless-init/inventory`: `serverless_*` fields in inventoryagent payload | ## What's in this PR **Agent changes (will land via the stacked PRs above):** - `ForceCollect()` added to `inventoryagent.Component` — fires before `modeConf.Runner()` so the inventory payload is sent before the container can scale to zero - `inventories_first_run_delay` config key to control startup delay - New `cmd/serverless-init/inventory` package: populates `serverless_*` fields (cloud provider, workload type, origin, resource name, deployment model, runtime, agent commit, DD config) into the inventoryagent payload - Enhanced startup diagnostics (`DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`) including UUID, CCRID, and inventory pipeline config **POC deploy scripts (`scripts/serverless-deploy/`, not intended to merge to main):** - Deploys 9 test services across GCP (Cloud Run Service/Job/Function) and Azure (Container App, Web App Containers, Web App SITECONTAINERS, Web App Linux Code) - `demo.sh` — one-command end-to-end runner: build → deploy all 9 → trigger cold starts → collect logs → print REDAPL SQL query ## How to run the POC ```bash export GCP_PROJECT=datadog-serverless-gcp-demo export AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<sub-id> export DD_API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev) export IMAGE_TAG=1.10.2-poc-$(date +%Y%m%d) cd scripts/serverless-deploy ./demo.sh ``` ###dd-auth command equivalent: `export DD_API_KEY=$(dd-auth vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev)` Or if it's wrapping the whole script: `dd-auth ./demo.sh ` Then paste the generated SQL into **go/redapl → Queries → SQL** to see the agents in `datadog_agent`. ## Key findings from 9-platform testing | Platform | UUID behaviour | `datadog_agent` rows | |---|---|---| | GCP Cloud Run | New UUID per cold start | `ForceCollect()` required — container scales to zero before 60s delay | | Azure Container App | Stable UUID per replica | Upserts same row reliably | | Azure Web App | DMI UUID from underlying VM | Apps on same App Service Plan share UUID → need CCRID-based PK | This motivates `serverless_init_agent` (SVLS-9604): a separate REDAPL table keyed by `resource_id` (CCRID) instead of Agent UUID. ## Not in scope for merge - `scripts/serverless-deploy/` — test infrastructure only, not shipped in the agent - `scripts/serverless-deploy/diagnostic-results-*.txt` — personal test output

signals.title: [NETPATH-1122] Add baseline Dynamic Tests for CNM (deprecated version)
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds opt-in baseline Dynamic Tests for Cloud Network Monitoring (CNM). Baseline mode selects a small, representative set of paths directly from each CNM connection snapshot when full connection-monitoring Dynamic Tests are disabled. Traceroute must also be enabled in the system-probe configuration. If full connection-monitoring Dynamic Tests are enabled, they take precedence and the collector continues to use standard scheduling. ### Motivation Hosts without full Dynamic Tests currently have no included Network Path coverage for observed CNM traffic. Baseline mode provides limited recurring path visibility. The selector favors connections that are more useful for diagnosis while keeping resource use predictable: timeout, RTO, and retransmit observations rank ahead of healthy traffic, then higher-volume connections rank first. ### Design and key changes #### Snapshot selection - Reuses the existing connection eligibility filters before ranking. - Selects at most three unique paths from each complete CNM snapshot. - Ranks diagnostic observations first, then total sent and received bytes, with the stable path hash as the final tie-breaker. - Keeps only the best three candidates while scanning, so selection memory remains bounded and connections are not aggregated. - Reconsiders a repeated path only when its later observation has a stronger score. #### Data boundary Both CNM producers populate the same generic `ConnectionSignals` structure on `NetworkPathConnection`: normalized timeout count, RTO count, retransmits, sent bytes, and received bytes. These are raw connection observations rather than baseline-specific derived state. The baseline selector in `baseline.go` is the only layer that interprets those signals into the diagnostic and traffic-volume ranking dimensions. This keeps producer behavior equivalent without coupling the shared connection model to baseline policy. #### Scheduling and payloads Standard, baseline, and NetFlow paths share the collector's existing eligibility checks, path construction, scheduling telemetry, deduplication, interval, TTL, context limit, and rate limit. Baseline mode adds only the snapshot-ranking step before selected paths enter that common machinery. Baseline results are recurring Dynamic Tests and carry `dynamic_test_profile: "baseline"` in Network Path payloads so downstream consumers can distinguish them from standard tests. Baseline-only operation also enables the collector and its reverse-DNS dependency. Baseline mode and Dynamic Remote Configuration filters are compatible and independent: baseline mode controls snapshot ranking, while the effective local-plus-RC filter controls path admission. When an RC rule admits the winning baseline candidate, its configuration ID, source, and tags are preserved alongside `dynamic_test_profile: "baseline"`. #### E2E coverage Adds a packaged-Agent E2E suite that generates CNM host traffic and verifies through fakeintake that a Network Path event is emitted with the baseline profile. The existing Remote Config host-traffic suite and the new baseline suite now share one fixture. The fixture replaces the GHCR-backed HTTP container and runtime `curl` installation with Python standard-library HTTP and traffic generation, including readiness checks, cleanup, and failure logs. ### Manual validation Use this minimal `datadog.yaml` configuration: ```yaml network_config: enabled: true network_path: connections_monitoring: baseline_tests_enabled: true ``` Enable traceroute in `system-probe.yaml`: ```yaml traceroute: enabled: true ``` After generating outbound TCP traffic from the host, verify that Network Path events are emitted with `test_run_type: "dynamic"` and `dynamic_test_profile: "baseline"`. Up to three unique eligible paths should be selected from each CNM snapshot, subject to the existing collector filters and scheduling limits. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test` - Added focused unit coverage for selection order, each diagnostic signal, sent/received byte derivation, repeated-path handling, configuration, producer signal mapping, payload serialization, and recurring scheduling cadence. - Added packaged-Agent E2E coverage for baseline Network Path events through fakeintake. ### Additional Notes The new configuration setting defaults to `false` and remains an internal rollout control omitted from generated `datadog.yaml` examples.

signals.title: fix(system-probe): protect module loader registry with mutex during Register

Fixes a data race on the module loader registry: `Register` wrote `l.cfg`, `l.stats`, and iterated `l.modules` without holding the loader mutex, racing with `GetStats` which takes the lock. signals.title: Report DDOT process state in the installer agent state
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `ddot_process_state` line to the agent state the fleet installer daemon reports through the remote-config client. It is set on the `datadog-agent` package entry, next to the existing stable/experiment version and config version. The state is read from `dd-procmgrd` over its socket (gRPC on a UDS on Linux, a named pipe on Windows — the `dd-procmgr` binary is never invoked) when the process manager supervises DDOT, and falls back to systemd on Linux / the service manager on Windows otherwise. This reuses `pkg/procmgr/coat`, which already performs exactly that collection for COAT telemetry and already carries a `ddot` entry in its service catalog; the new `Snapshot.ServiceProcessState` only maps a collected snapshot onto a reported value. Reported values: `running`, `starting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `created`, `crashed`, `exited`, `failed` when procmgr supervises DDOT; `running` when the legacy systemd unit or Windows service is active; `not_installed` when DDOT is absent; `unknown` when procmgr owns it but is unreachable; and `""` only when nothing can be determined, so the backend can tell "not reported" from "no DDOT on this host". The probe is bounded (2s) and cannot fail a state refresh — it returns a string only, never an error. ### Motivation The update monitoring uses the reported agent state to decide whether an update succeeded. Now that DDOT can be updated on its own (version or config), the state had no way to express whether the DDOT process actually came back up afterwards. This matters because a broken DDOT does not end an experiment by itself: the core agent does not read `otel-config.yaml`, so the experiment agent stays healthy, and `dd-procmgrd` retries a failing child forever rather than giving up. The reported process state is therefore the only signal that can tell the backend not to promote. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests: - `pkg/procmgr/coat/process_state_test.go` — every `pb.ProcessState`, both legacy supervisor modes, not-installed, procmgr-unreachable, installed-without-supervisor, unknown service ID. - `pkg/fleet/daemon/ddot_state_test.go` — the collector seam (nil collector, procmgr running/failed, systemd, not-installed) and a `refreshState` test asserting the field lands only on the `datadog-agent` entry. - `pkg/fleet/daemon/local_api_test.go` — the field round-trips through the local API `/status`. Ran: `bazel test //pkg/procmgr/coat:coat_test //pkg/fleet/daemon:daemon_test`, `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/proto/pbgo/core` (msgp round-trip), `bazel build //cmd/installer/...`, `dda inv linter.go`. Generated protobuf code is committed and `dda inv protobuf.generate` is a no-op on the tree. E2E — new `TestDDOTConfigFailureReportsFailedAndReverts` in the fleet config suite (Linux, runs in the existing `new-e2e-fleet-config` job with no CI wiring changes): 1. Install the agent and the `ddot` extension; assert DDOT healthy under `dd-procmgrd`, launched with the stable `otel-config.yaml`, reported as `running`. 2. Start a config experiment patching `/otel-config.yaml` with an invalid debug-exporter verbosity; assert the broken config reaches the experiment collector and DDOT is unhealthy. 3. Assert the reported `ddot_process_state` becomes `failed`. 4. Assert nothing promoted it: `experiment_config_version` still set, `stable_config_version` unchanged, stable config free of the bad value. 5. Mimic the backend reacting to that state by sending the revert task (`stop_experiment_config`). 6. Assert the revert landed: `experiment_config_version` cleared, `stable_config_version` never changed, stable `otel-config.yaml` restored byte-for-byte, DDOT healthy under `dd-procmgrd` on the stable config, reported state back to `running`. ### Additional Notes - **The failure state is `failed`, not `crashed`.** `CRASHED` exists in the proto and Go enums but the Rust process manager never emits it: `set_last_status` maps any non-zero exit or signal to `Failed`. - **`restart: on-failure` never gives up on DDOT.** With `restart_sec: 2`, backoff ×2 capped at 60s, and `start_limit_burst: 5` over a 10s window, attempts land at t≈0, 2, 6, 14, 30, 62… — never 5 within any 10s window, so DDOT loops `Failed → Starting → Failed` indefinitely and `dd-procmgrd` stays up. - Field 17 is new, so older backends skip it and newer backends see `""` from older agents. The msgp decoder skips unknown fields, so mixed-version marshalling is safe. - During a version experiment, `Installed`/`ProcmgrConfigured` are resolved from the daemon's own install root while the process state comes from the shared procmgr socket. That only affects the `unknown`-vs-`stopped` distinction; the running state stays correct, since the stable and experiment procmgr share one socket and the DDOT process definition filename is invariant (only `${DD_CONF_DIR}` differs).

signals.title: fix(e2e): CentOS 7 yum vault mirrors
signals.text: <!-- dd-meta {"pullId":"a1690776-5acc-42ba-b967-8f9ed1ebf680","source":"chat","resourceId":"3ccc3ce3-feac-4128-956d-32085850139b","workflowId":"033bd140-0f89-4a0a-9a1b-d6aa324a0839","codeChangeId":"033bd140-0f89-4a0a-9a1b-d6aa324a0839","sourceType":"slack"} --> ### What does this PR do? Fixes CentOS 7 E2E jobs on `main` that are red because the OS is EOL. On CentOS 7 the stock `/centos/7/` path on `vault.centos.org` now returns `HTTP 403`, so any `yum` transaction that must refresh the `base`/`updates`/`extras` metadata fails with `No more mirrors to try`. See incident-59302 Two jobs are affected today: - `new-e2e-installer` — `(*Host).InstallDocker()` runs `sudo yum install -y docker`; docker never installs and the failure surfaces confusingly as the cleanup defer's `systemctl start docker` → **"Failed to start docker.service: Unit not found."** - `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-centos-a7-x86_64` (incident 59303) — `sudo yum install -y datadog-agent-ddot` fails refreshing the same CentOS base repo. This adds `(*Host).ConfigureYumMirrors()` in `test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host/host.go`, the yum-side counterpart to the existing `ConfigureAptMirrors()`. On CentOS 7 it rewrites `/etc/yum.repos.d/CentOS-Base.repo` so `base`/`updates`/`extras` each list three baseurls with `failovermethod=priority`, tried in order: 1. `http://vault.centos.org/7.9.2009/{os,updates,extras}/$basearch/` — canonical archive (primary) 2. `https://linuxsoft.cern.ch/centos-vault/7.9.2009/...` — CERN mirror (fallback) 3. `https://archive.kernel.org/centos-vault/7.9.2009/...` — kernel.org mirror (fallback) plus `skip_if_unavailable=1` and `timeout=30` (fail fast / degrade gracefully instead of hanging until the 2h job timeout), `gpgcheck=1` against the on-box CentOS-7 key, then `yum clean all`. Explicit baseurls are required because the old `mirror.centos.org` / `mirrorlist.centos.org` services were removed at EOL, so a mirrorlist is not an option. It is called from each suite's `SetupSuite`, before the first yum operation: - `test/new-e2e/tests/installer/unix/all_packages_test.go` and `.../script/all_scripts_test.go` (job `new-e2e-installer`) - `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-platform/tests/ddot_install_test.go` (job `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-centos-a7-x86_64`) — this suite already builds an `installer/host.Host`, so the fix is reused as-is. The helper is guarded to `Flavor == CentOS && Version starts with "7"`, so it no-ops on RHEL/Amazon Linux and on the CentOS 6 jobs (which use a different vault tree). We keep using `vault.centos.org` (the correct registry for EOL CentOS); `InstallDocker()` and the ddot install path are otherwise unchanged. ### Motivation Both jobs are red on `main`, and both root-cause to the same external event: CentOS 7 EOL / `vault.centos.org` returning 403 on the `/centos/7/` path, so every run fails regardless of the commit. The earlier apt-mirror hardening (#54459) had no yum/CentOS equivalent — this closes that gap and covers the agent-platform ddot suite that shares the same `Host` helper. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Confirmed the failure signature via CI: `new-e2e-installer` jobs (`1945363716`, `1944844242`, `1945267523`) and `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-centos-a7-x86_64` jobs (as recent as 2026-08-17) all show `CentOS-7 - Base` / `HTTPS Error 403 - Forbidden` / `No more mirrors to try` on `centos_79`. - Chose the primary URL from in-repo precedent: `pkg/util/kernel/headers/download/rpm/centos.go` uses the same `http://vault.centos.org/7.9.2009/{os,updates}/$basearch/` path in production (hence `http` + gpgcheck against the on-box key). - Verified the CERN and kernel.org fallbacks are the external mirrors listed on `vault.centos.org`'s own index and mirror the full `7.9.2009/` tree (paths map directly). They sit behind vault via `failovermethod=priority`; they are best-effort, not SLA-backed. - Verified the affected suites explicitly opt into internet via `ec2.WithInternetAccess()`, so the archives are reachable during setup. - Scoped via a `Flavor == CentOS && Version` prefix guard; confirmed no new imports, no BUILD.bazel changes, gofmt-safe indentation, balanced braces, and that `InstallDocker()` is byte-identical to `main`. - A local compile/lint check and a live reachability probe were not possible in this sandbox (pinned Go toolchain unavailable; outbound to vault blocked). The affected E2E jobs are the end-to-end validators. ### Additional Notes - Not covered here (same root cause, larger change): `new-e2e-agent-platform-step-by-step-centos-a7-x86_64` is also failing, but `stepByStepSuite` does not use `installer/host` and would need extra plumbing to call the helper. The `rpm-centos6` job is CentOS 6 (different vault tree) and is intentionally excluded by the version guard. Happy to extend to step-by-step in a follow-up or here if desired. - Because CentOS 7 vault content is frozen (no further security updates), the robust long-term fix is a one-time `reposync` of the tree into an owned artifact store (Artifactory/S3/Pulp, ~50 GB) with the fleet pointed at that — out of scope here, noted for follow-up. - Residual gap worth a reviewer's eye: the in-repo production reference exercises `/os/` and `/updates/`; `/extras/` (which provides the `docker` package) is part of the same `7.9.2009` tree but isn't independently proven in-repo — CI will confirm. --- PR by Bits - [View session in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/code/3ccc3ce3-feac-4128-956d-32085850139b) Comment @datadog to request changes
