signals.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signals.title: feat(ndm): add the workloadbalancing component
signals.text: ## What New `comp/workloadbalancing` component. Subscribes to the shared `HA_AGENT` Remote Config product for per-device workload balancing assignments, distinguished from HA Agent's own documents by an explicit `type` field. - **Registration is unconditional**: it always listens on `HA_AGENT` and reports apply status for its own documents, independent of the local `agent_workload_balancing.enabled` flag. That flag only gates `IsGroupActive`'s effect — nothing calls it yet, that's a following PR. - **Fallback owner**: when `comp/haagent` is disabled on an agent, `comp/workloadbalancing` reports status for anything that doesn't match its own discriminator too, so a document is never silently dropped by both sides. - **Malformed-but-present documents**: reported as an apply-status error *and* keep the group's previous assignment rather than clearing it, since "malformed" isn't the same as "removed." - Wired only into the three binaries that actually run the check-execution worker pool `IsGroupActive` will gate: `cmd/agent/subcommands/run`, `cmd/cluster-agent/subcommands/start`, and `cmd/cluster-agent-cloudfoundry/subcommands/run`. Not `diagnose`, `flare`, `jmx`, `snmp`, `check`, `dogstatsd`, `serverless-init`, or `systray`: none of those run checks through that worker pool, so there's nothing for the component to do there. ## Not in scope here - Nothing reads `IsGroupActive` yet — no effect on check execution until the worker-gating PR. - SNMP's instance-level config field, metric emission, and inventory metadata are separate, following PRs. - The RC schema itself lives in `dd-source`, coordinated separately. ## Testing Unit tests cover: valid assignment (active/standby), malformed-but-present (error + keeps prior state), fallback-owner both ways (HA Agent enabled/disabled), the local flag being off (document still claimed and reported, `IsGroupActive` still `true`), a group's assignment clearing once its document stops appearing in a later poll, and the RC listener always registering regardless of the local flag. > **Note:** This PR was created by Claude

signals.title: Enables the v3 metrics intake for series in DDOT
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Enables the **v3 metrics intake for series** in DDOT (the `otel-agent` binary). ### Motivation OTAGENT-1130, under epic OTAGENT-1133 ("Reduce customer metrics egress bandwidth 30–50% with v3 payload"). DDOT was the last OTel surface still on the v2 series intake. This PR moves DDOT onto the v3 series path, aligning it with the core Agent (series v3 default since 7.81). ### Describe how you validated your changes - **Unit:** `cmd/otel-agent/config` tests pass; the guard tests now assert the resolved value is `datadog_only`. - **Static:** `dda inv linter.go` — 0 issues; `dda inv otel-agent.build` — OK. - **Manual (local, standalone otel-agent → fakeintake, `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=true`, zstd):** series routed to `/api/intake/metrics/v3/series` and **0** on `/api/v2/series`; all payloads zstd (wire magic `28b52ffd`); v3 payloads decode correctly; a cumulative Sum arrived as a delta `COUNT` (c2d); sketches stayed on `/api/beta/sketches` (v2). - **Manual + telemetrygen + delta** - metrics are posted to https://api.datadoghq.com/api/intake/metrics/v3/series" (202 Accepted) - **Manual + telemetrygen + cumulative** - metrics are converted to delta & posted to https://api.datadoghq.com/api/intake/metrics/v3/series" (202 Accepted) - **E2E:** new `TestOTelAgentV3Series` (KinD DDOT with v3 enabled) asserts OTLP metrics reach the intake, series land on the v3 endpoint (`RouteStats`), and v3 payloads are zstd. Auto-wired into the `new-e2e-otel` job — no CI changes. (Runs in CI on this PR.) ### Additional Notes - **Kill-switch / rollout:** enablement follows `use_v3_api.series.enabled` (default `datadog_only`). v2 remains the compat/fallback path (non-Datadog destinations, non-zstd builds, non-migrated regions). Opt out with `use_v3_api.series.enabled=false` (or `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=false`). - **Scope:** series only. Sketches (distributions) stay on v2 (v3 for sketches is a separate opt-in). - **Known follow-up (this PR):** the auto-injected `datadog/dd-autoconfigured` flare extension keeps its own zlib serializer and now logs a benign but misleading "disabling v3 metrics intake" warning — the same warning #52301 suppressed on the OSS path, surfaced because v3 is now enabled in-process. Egress is unaffected (verified v3 + zstd); the warning does not reflect the actual series path. To be addressed. - this deliberately does **not** revert #52301 (`serializerexporter/serializer.go`). That line only runs for the OSS Datadog exporter in opentelemetry-collector-contrib - for case "datadog_only" - the PR updates "use_v3_api.series.endpoints" by "https://api.xxxx" https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1130

signals.title: [BARX-2009] Drop Agent 6 RC tags on Go modules
signals.text: ## Motivation - Agent releases create a nested Go module tag for every release candidate. These tags significantly increase the repository's tag count and add pressure to GitHub and GitLab. Agent 7 already drops creating these RC module tags; this PR applies the same behavior to Agent 6. See the [RFC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15XFZ4AKy8Yhyruo7zilTR84j5kV1dI5eFBhoEFfGzhI/edit?tab=t.0) for more info. ## Important Note - Agent 6 RC module dependencies use versions backed by RC tags. After removing those tags, the dependencies must use another resolvable version. We use pseudo-versions derived from the release branch commit, ensuring modules in the same RC can consume each other’s changes without creating nested RC tags. ## Changes - Skip nested Go module tag creation for Agent 6 release candidates. - Resolve Agent 6 RC internal module dependencies to canonical pseudo-versions at the current release branch commit. - Cache each resolved pseudo-version while updating module requirements. - Keep final Agent 6 release tags - Document the Agent 6 RC pseudo-version workflow. - Add unit coverage for tag suppression and pseudo-version dependency updates. ## Tests - `dda inv invoke-unit-tests.run --tests=release` (46 tests passed) - `GITLAB_CI=true dda inv linter.python` - `git diff --check`

signals.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process can not resolve secret handles and expects to receive them from the core agent already resolved ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

The Python extension selects its standard library list on `is_python_3.14`, which earlier versions do not define. {#v2-3-0-fixed} ##### Fixed - Fixed `py_binary_rule_builder()` / `py_test_rule_builder()` (from `python/api/executables.bzl`) failing at analysis time with a visibility error when used to construct a custom rule from an external module. - (compile\_pip\_requirements) Add the explicit `data` attribute and forward it directly to the generated `py_binary`, so files passed via `data` can be referenced from `extra_args` using `$(location ...)`. - (coverage) The warning about a missing bundled `coverage.py` wheel is no longer emitted as we are now falling back to a pure python wheel ([#​3950](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3950)). - (gazelle) The Python extension now uses the correct standard library module list for `python_version` 3.13 and 3.14; previously both fell back to the 3.11 list, so modules added or removed since then (e.g. `compression.zstd`, `telnetlib`) were misclassified. The fallback list for unrecognized versions is now the newest available one rather than 3.11 ([#​3978](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/3978)). - (pypi) Allow `uv_lock` to be specified in `pip.parse` without requiring `requirements_lock` (or other os-specific requirement file attributes) to be set. - (pypi) Fixed the fixed-point loop that resolves self-referencing extras (`pkg[extra]` entries in a package's own `Requires-Dist`). The loop compared the number of extras discovered in the current round against the number known before it, rather than against the size of the merged set. As a result it could stop before every extra was resolved, silently dropping dependencies only reachable through two or more `pkg[extra]` hops, and for the common case of a package with no self-referencing extras it never converged at all, running all 10000 rounds while evaluating each wheel's generated `BUILD` file ([#​4039](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/4039)). - (pypi) Requirement `--hash=<algo>:<digest>` pins and Simple API `#<algo>=<digest>` URL fragments are now parsed for all hash algorithms instead of silently dropping everything except `sha256`. Non-sha256 pins are matched against the digests advertised by the index and downloads are verified using the corresponding Subresource Integrity value, and the pins are kept in the requirement line when falling back to `pip` ([#​3972](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3972)). As part of this, `whl_library` repos created by `pip.parse` now always pass the digest via the `integrity` attribute (SRI format) instead of `sha256`, and the lock file facts store digests as `<algo>:<digest>` values (the facts version was bumped, so cached index information is refreshed once). - (pypi) `pip.parse(uv_lock = ...)` no longer exposes uv workspace/root members that resolve to no wheel or sdist (e.g. `source = { virtual = "." }` or editable installs). Previously these source-less packages were added to the hub's `all_requirements` / `all_whl_requirements` with an alias to a subpackage that does not exist, breaking analysis for anything enumerating the full set such as `modules_mapping(wheels = all_whl_requirements)` ([#​3934](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3934)). - (pypi) correctly parse the `index_url` for each wheel so that the source registry is forwarded to the {obj}`whl_library`. This is so that the `purl` for `package_metadata` can be correctly constructed. - (pypi) fixed the URL normalization function to correctly handle local paths enabling wheel sources files to point to an absolute path. Currently it supports the `file://<absolute_path>` for linux and windows like paths. We also support envsubst for the said paths from now on. {#v2-3-0-added} ##### Added - (bzlmod) Added MODULE.bazel flag aliases for Starlark-defined flags: `build_python_zip`, `incompatible_default_to_explicit_init_py`, `python_path`, and `experimental_python_import_all_repositories`. - (bzlmod) Added the `{obj}`explicit\_init\_py`` tag class to the `{obj}`config`` module extension for configuring implicit `__init__.py` file generation module-wide. ([#​3997](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/3997), [#​2945](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/2945)) - (cc) Added experimental {obj}`py_extension` macro for creating C/C++ Python extension modules ([#​3283](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3283)). (cc) Added `libc`, `platform_machine`, `platform_tag`, `soabi`, and `sys_platform` attributes and info fields to {obj}`py_cc_toolchain` / {obj}`PyCcToolchainInfo`. - (pip,python) Added `pyproject_toml` attribute to {obj}`pip.default`, {obj}`pip.parse` and {obj}`python.defaults` to read the default Python version from the `requires-python` field of `pyproject.toml`. - (py\_test) Added an opt-in safeguard against `py_test` targets that silently pass without running any tests. Set {obj}`--@rules_python//python/config_settings:validate_test_main=enabled` to fail the build when a test's main module only contains inert top-level statements (definitions, imports, assignments) and never invokes a test runner ([#​3824](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3824)). {#v2-2-0} </details> --- ### Configuration 📅 **Schedule**: (in timezone Europe/Paris) - Branch creation - At 12:00 AM through 04:59 AM and 10:00 PM through 11:59 PM, Monday through Friday (`* 0-4,22-23 * * 1-5`) - Only on Sunday and Saturday (`* * * * 0,6`) - Automerge - At any time (no schedule defined) 🚦 **Automerge**: Disabled by config. signals.title: Add concurrency test for flare archive name uniqueness
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? * Adds a test that races many goroutines through `getArchiveName()` in `comp/core/flare/helpers/builder.go`, asserting no two calls ever produce the same archive filename. * Update the changelog to include changes from #54911 No production code changes: #54911's PID+counter suffix already guarantees this, but it was only covered by a single-threaded, same-timestamp test (`TestGetArchiveNameIsUniqueWithinSameSecond`). This adds a companion test that exercises real concurrent callers instead. ### Motivation We considered reverting #54911 in favor of relying on a higher-precision timestamp alone, but a concurrency test proved that `time.Now()`'s effective resolution is not a reliable uniqueness mechanism on its own — even on Linux, concurrent goroutines can read the identical nanosecond value. #54911's PID+counter suffix is what actually guarantees uniqueness, so we're keeping it as-is and locking in the guarantee with a test that mirrors the real production race: the `/agent/flare` HTTP handler and the remote-config listener independently calling `Save()` around the same time. Jira: FLREM-148, FLREM-150 ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/flare/... --no-cache --race`, repeated multiple times, all passing.

signals.title: [AAD-6] Unify detector point windows
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? > [!NOTE] > 1. This is mostly for metrics that arrive every 15s, I'm thinking about how to properly manage logs that are every 1s in a future PR (instead of a 30m retention they have 2m retention this way) -> [comment](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024#discussion_r3802840340). > 2. The end goal is to unify storage when we do the warmup, some values are duplicated (future PR). This unifies all detectors (except RRCF) with an interface to get the min / max number of points per series. This way there is no discrepancy with the storage max retention (now deduced by default [1]). Warmup lazy behavior: Max retention behavior [2]: Detectors follow these conditions: 1. A new series has < min points -> no detector state created (discarded) 2. A new series has min points -> create initial state 3. The series has > min and < max points -> process + can trigger anomalies 4. The series has < min points now but had before > min points -> process (update state only if needed) but don't trigger anomalies 5. Internal detector states have max MaxPoints state points (we don't have a state for a point not present in the storage) 6. A new series can't have > max points nor > max state points (eviction) It improves memory / CPU since series that have few points don't have state, it's lazy computation. It's a tradeoff but it makes more sense to not save the states of points that are stale. Extra changes: - Bocpd has less points: (120, 200) -> (60, 120) - Added all the min / max points to the config Benchmark (all detectors enabled): Overall metric | Baseline | Changed | Delta -- | -- | -- | -- In-use heap, average | 261.02 MB | 135.29 MB | **-48.16%** Detector-phase time, average | 10.751 s | 9.835 s | **-8.52%** Macro F1 | 0.265206 | 0.267651 | +0.92% Macro precision | 0.332990 | 0.491846 | +47.70% Macro recall | 0.578832 | 0.511810 | -11.58% Predictions | 682 | 420 | -38.42% ### Motivation Memory / cpu optimization + unify detectors ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes [1] The max retention time is based on 15s / point -> `15 * max(detectors.MaxPoints) + 16` seconds [2] This is enforced by the retention time deduced by the max points for each detector so storage is always big enough We need to fine tune again to improve the scores (all detectors enabled): Scenario | F1 baseline → changed | Detector phase | Heap -- | -- | -- | -- block-building-outage | 0.285714 → 0.000000 | 22.3 → 9.7 ms | 194.7 → 39.2 MB byzantine-fault-cascade | 0 → 0 | 128.815 → 117.926 s | 1216.5 → 1219.1 MB cascading-regional-outage | 0.063224 → 0.000000 | 9.2 → 5.4 ms | 165.7 → 29.3 MB cassandra-repair-degradation | 0.318046 → 0.641981 | 48.2 → 19.5 ms | 294.8 → 62.6 MB dns-upstream-outage | 0.052606 → 0.025667 | 14.0 → 6.5 ms | 182.9 → 46.3 MB kafka-partition-saturation | 0.117641 → 0.108369 | 32.8 → 20.4 ms | 248.4 → 55.1 MB lock-contention-cascade | 0.971969 → 0.365964 | 8.9 → 3.6 ms | 141.5 → 45.4 MB memcached-eviction-storm | 0.057796 → 0.115670 | 13.5 → 4.2 ms | 129.6 → 26.8 MB pool-exhaustion | 0.093612 → 0.097034 | 9.2 → 5.5 ms | 119.1 → 15.9 MB redis-billing-latency | 0.604642 → 0.928561 | 17.6 → 9.4 ms | 185.9 → 32.6 MB redis-cpu-saturation | 0.615742 → 0.928561 | 13.7 → 5.6 ms | 147.2 → 32.6 MB tiered-cascading-outage | 0.001476 → 0.000000 | 10.1 → 3.7 ms | 106.0 → 18.6 MB

signals.title: Pass the lint build tags to --only-modified-packages discovery
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Passes the build tags `golangci-lint` will use to the package discovery done by `dda inv linter.go --only-modified-packages`. ### Motivation `linter.go` passes no build tags, so `process_input_args` turns them into `[]` and `get_modified_packages` skips its `go list` filter (gated on `if build_tags:` since #54890). A modified package whose files are all excluded by the lint tags is then handed to `golangci-lint` as an explicit target, and the run fails with: ``` level=error msg="[linters_context] typechecking error: build constraints exclude all Go files in .../pkg/security/tests/syscall_tester/go" ``` A `./pkg/...` wildcard skips such packages silently, an explicit package name does not, which is why CI (explicit `--targets`, recursive) is unaffected and only the `go-linter` pre-push hook fails. Callers that intentionally pass no tags, such as the Bazel-driven test task, keep skipping the filter. ### Describe how you validated your changes On a branch that modifies `pkg/security/tests/syscall_tester/go`, whose only file is behind `//go:build syscalltesters`: - before: the hook fails with the error above - after: `All linters passed`, and the target list is identical to the one produced before #54890 ### Additional Notes Only affects `--only-modified-packages`, which CI does not use.

signals.title: CONTINT-5289 - retry reaching kubelet with HTTPS
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? When setting up the kubelet client if we fail to reach it using HTTPS, we try to reach it using HTTP. In this case, when a component requests the global kubelet client, this one is configured with HTTP, try to set it up with HTTPS again. In case of failure to reach it with HTTPS, return the kubelet client set up with HTTP, this is fine we'll retry later. In case of real failure return an error, we don't want to continue, this is ok as anyway if we kept the old client we'll reach some errors at some point too. In case we succeed, we never retry anymore. ### Motivation users getting stuck with an HTTP connection due to transient error at start, now will benefit from HTTPS connection after some retry. ### Describe how you validated your changes unit test with mock kubelet that denies HTTPS at start then allows it and validate the new client using HTTPS afterward. ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [FA] Back up agent configuration files at every agent start
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Implements the plan in `config-backup-plan.md`: every time the core Agent starts, it writes a byte-exact snapshot of the configuration files it actually loaded into a dedicated directory (`<confdir>/config-backups`). This is a **config-provenance and audit record** — a byte-exact history of the configuration each Agent actually started with, including layers the installer does not own (hand edits, mounted `conf.d`, fleet policies, operator-templated files). It is **not** a disaster-recovery backup. ### Storage layout - Content-addressed archives: `<sha256>.tar.gz` + `<sha256>.manifest.json` sidecar (manifest renamed first, so a visible archive always has a manifest). - Append-only occurrence log `starts.jsonl` (one line per start), capped by line count. - `flock`-based rotation with a 2s timeout; never skips the snapshot, only rotation. - Content-addressed naming means an unchanged config writes zero bytes however many times it restarts, and re-seeing a config never re-writes the archive. ### Component - New `comp/core/configbackup` (`def`/`fx`/`impl`), `// team: fleet-automation`, wired into `cmd/agent/subcommands/run` only (never in `comp/core/bundle.go`, so `agent status`/`agent config` never write a snapshot). - The module forces its own construction with `fx.Invoke` (the `configsync` pattern), because the component exposes no public method. - `OnStart` hook, so it runs after every constructor — right for the provenance goal, wrong for crash-forensics (a config that fails inside the config constructor never reaches it; the installer's transactional design already is the pre-experiment backup). ### Settings (schema, public) `config_backup.enabled` (true), `config_backup.max_snapshots` (10), `config_backup.max_starts_logged` (1000), `config_backup.directory` (empty — derived from `ConfigFileUsed()` so `${conf_path}` (which does not follow `-c`) can never send experiment snapshots into the stable dir). ### Installer integration - `copyDirectory` (Linux) now skips `config-backups` (required for promote correctness + removes the nesting hazard). Windows is already safe via the `*.yaml` robocopy mask; a test pins that. - `getConfigFileSpec` refuses any path under `config-backups`, including the `/managed` fallback branch (loophole closed). ### Extra surfaces - Flare provider: ships manifests + `starts.jsonl` only, never the archives (they contain verbatim config copies including secrets). - `agent config backup list`: read-only listing (digest, timestamp, deployment ID, size) joined against `starts.jsonl`. Validates archive content digest against the name, rejects unsafe entry names, caps decompressed bytes/entry count (gzip-bomb bound). ### Security - No component running as root and no installer path ever reads these archives (restore is out of scope and belongs in the installer with its own threat model). - Manifest records real uid/gid/mode per file so a future restore path must confront that it cannot restore root-owned files from a `dd-agent`-written archive. - `0700` dir / `0600` files (nix), SYSTEM+Administrators ACL (Windows), flare ships manifests only. ## Deviations from the plan (flagging for review) 1. **Module structure**: the plan says `def`/`fx`/`impl` each with their own `go.mod`. The component needs `comp/core/sysprobeconfig/def` and `pkg/util/hostname` (both root-module packages) for the CWS policies dir and hostname, which a separate nested module cannot import (cycle). So it is a **root-module component**, exactly like `configstream` (the plan's own sibling reference for the forcing pattern). No `modules.yml` entry. 2. **`is_experiment`**: the plan says "never inferred from the directory path". On Linux the only signal available to the core Agent is the installer's `-exp` dir naming, so this uses `strings.HasSuffix(resolvedSrcDir, "-exp")`; on Windows it is always `false` (the live dir is always the stable one). `deployment_id` comes from `.deployment-id` as the plan requires. 3. **E2E assertion**: the plan's "experiment dir holds the pre-experiment snapshot" relies on `cp -a` copying the history into the experiment dir, which **contradicts** the plan's own "Required, not optional: exclude `config-backups` from `copyDirectory`". I kept the exclusion (per the explicit requirement) and the E2E test asserts the experiment Agent's own snapshot instead. This tension is worth a decision before merge — see the recorded objection in the plan about the out-of-tree store. ## Testing - Unit tests (16) in `comp/core/configbackup/impl`: file selection/exclusions, symlink-not-read-through, external-tree prefix, content-addressed dedup, A/B/A/B flap (2 archives, 4 log lines), rotation never-evict rules, permissions, read-only dir, flock contention, stale tmp cleanup, truncated-archive detection, `ConfigFileUsed()==""` not writing to `.`. - Installer tests: `getConfigFileSpec` refuses `/config-backups/*` and `/managed/config-backups/*`; `copyDirectory` skips `config-backups`; Windows `*.yaml` mask test. - `dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd` passes; smoke-tested the built agent (snapshot + manifest + starts.jsonl written, `agent config backup list` works). - E2E test added to the existing `tests/fleet` config suite (Linux-only). **Not run** — requires AWS infra; CI job already covers `./tests/fleet`. - Lints: `lint-components`, `lint-fxutil-oneshot-test`, `github.lint-codeowner`, `linter.go` on the new-e2e fleet target — all pass. ## Open questions for reviewers 1. The `copyDirectory` exclusion vs. the "pre-experiment snapshot in the experiment dir" goal — which behavior is wanted? (The plan is internally contradictory here.) 2. Should `security-agent.yaml`, `system-probe.yaml`, `application_monitoring.yaml` be excluded or scrubbed from v1 (they are root-owned and not `dd-agent`-writable)? 3. `is_experiment` heuristic — acceptable, or should the out-of-tree store be revisited instead? --- ## Sub-agent review findings (3 parallel reviewers) Three reviewer sub-agents reviewed the diff (component correctness/security, installer lifecycle, tests/CLI/E2E). Findings and dispositions: ### Applied in follow-up commit `7fab22183c` - **HIGH (component)** — `evictSnapshots` never evicted orphaned archives (those whose start records were trimmed or never written), so `max_snapshots` was not a hard bound and orphans inflated `toEvict`. Now candidates are built from every archive on disk. Added a test. - **HIGH (tests)** — E2E `promote-keeps-history` assertion was trivially satisfied by the pre-existing stable snapshot. Now asserts the count strictly grows. - **MEDIUM (component)** — archive temp file was not `fsync`ed before rename; a crash could leave a zero/partial archive under the final name. Added `tmp.Sync()`. - **MEDIUM (installer)** — `copyRegularFile` failed hard on `os.Lchown` EPERM when running as non-root; now logs and continues, matching `cp -a`. - **LOW (component)** — `walkTree` used `d.Type()` which can misreport regular files on filesystems without `d_type`; now uses `info.Mode().IsRegular()`. - **MEDIUM (tests)** — added unit tests for the full `backup()` happy path, `enabled=false`, the `directory` override, and the positive digest-verification path. - **LOW (tests)** — E2E count check moved inside `EventuallyWithT` to avoid a publish race. ### Disputed (reviewer error, verified) - Installer reviewer claimed `delete`/`delete-all` bypass the `config-backups` guard. **Incorrect**: `getConfigFileSpec` is consulted at the top of `FileOperation.apply` for all operation types, so delete is refused too (verified with a test). ### Left as open questions (design decisions, not mechanical fixes) - **HIGH (installer)** — Linux `replaceConfigDirectory` deletes the old stable's `config-backups` on promote (renames stable to a temp dir, then `RemoveAll`s it). With the `copyDirectory` exclusion, the promoted stable therefore holds only the experiment's own snapshots; the pre-experiment history is lost on promote. The plan's "history is continuous" goal needs a decision: preserve/merge the old stable history across promote (e.g. rename it into the new stable's `config-backups`), or accept the loss and rely on the out-of-tree store from the plan's recorded objection. **This is the single most important open question.** - **MEDIUM (installer)** — `copyDirectory` is not a full `cp -a` equivalent (no hard links, timestamps, xattrs/ACLs, setuid/setgid/sticky). Likely fine for a config dir; documenting. - **LOW (component)** — `cleanStaleTmp` can delete a concurrent publish's temp file (runs without the rotation lock); archive-exists check treats any non-IsNotExist error as "exists". - **NIT** — `config_backup` schema section has no `full-agent-only` tag; `backup list` surfaces on `cluster-agent config backup list` (harmless, prints "no backups found").

signals.title: fix(e2e): Avoid secret propagation to copy file paths
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Removes secret propagation from the temporary pathname generated by `CopyInlineFile` while preserving secrecy on the inline file contents. This prevents the pathname from tainting the `CopyFile` triggers array as secret and allows Pulumi to serialize the remote copy resource during previews. ### Motivation Inline Agent configuration includes secret values such as the API key. Because the temporary pathname is produced by an `ApplyT` on that content, Pulumi marks the pathname secret even though it contains no file contents. Passing that secret pathname through the remote copy triggers caused previews to fail with `malformed RPC secret: missing value for "triggers"`. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Ran `dda inv test --module=./test/e2e-framework --targets=./components/command/...`. - Reproduced the preview failure with both Pulumi CLI 3.257.0 and 3.253.0 before the change. - Ran `dda inv aws.create-vm --use-fakeintake` after the change. Pulumi preview completed and the update successfully created all 29 resources, including the EC2 host, healthy fakeintake ECS service, and running Agent.

signals.title: Add PostgreSQL collector for Config Files Discovery
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds a PostgreSQL collector to Config Files Discovery (`comp/core/configfilesdiscovery`), modeled on the Redis collector added in #54375. It collects: - `postgresql.conf`, resolved via (in order) an explicit `config_file` argv setting, an explicit `-D` data directory, or a `PGDATA`-derived fallback (`$PGDATA/postgresql.conf`). No default path is hardcoded — without an explicit source or a usable `PGDATA`, no file is collected. - A small allow-listed set of non-secret environment variables: `PGDATA`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD`, `POSTGRES_INITDB_WALDIR`. Everything else — passwords, `PGSSL*`, `DATABASE_URL`, `POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS`, etc. — is excluded by an explicit deny-list on top of the shared secret-name filter. Ambiguous or conflicting config sources (e.g. differing `-D` values across live processes, or an explicit-but-empty `config_file`) block collection rather than guessing. Also: - Registers the collector in `fx.go`. - Regenerates the affected `BUILD.bazel` files via gazelle/buildifier. - Extends the Docker E2E discovery suite with a Postgres fixture (`postgres:16`, pinned by digest via the ECR pull-through cache) and `TestPostgresConfigFilePayloadSentToEventPlatform`, verifying the payload, allowed env vars, and that no password-shaped variable is ever forwarded. ## Motivation Extends Config Files Discovery's existing Redis/Kafka coverage to PostgreSQL. ## Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — all unit tests pass. - `dda inv linter.go` — clean. - `dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd` — builds successfully. - `bazel build //comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — succeeds. - Opening as a **draft** to let the Docker E2E discovery suite run in CI (the live/local run against provisioned AWS infra was not run locally). ## Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs - Uses `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_PROPERTIES` since no dedicated PostgreSQL payload format enum exists yet. - Only launch commands that literally exec `postgres` are recognized; custom wrappers that never exec it are unsupported. - Host/systemd PostgreSQL is unsupported (Config Files Discovery has no `RuntimeHost` reader). - `*_FILE` variants (e.g. `POSTGRES_DB_FILE`) and locale/timezone/`POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS` variables are intentionally not allow-listed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: APM: Fix pkg/trace log format-string bugs
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fix format-string bugs in `pkg/trace` and add `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/trace/log` to the govet `printf` `funcs` allowlist in `.golangci.yml` so this class of bug is caught by CI going forward. ### Motivation pkg/trace logger has printf style commands but the govet rule didn't know about this so there were a few spots where the printf directives were wrong ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv linter.go --module=pkg/trace` → `0 issues.` / `All linters passed` (after all fixes; before the fixes it reported the 5 originally-known findings plus 2 additional `%s`-with-non-Stringer findings, all now fixed). - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/trace/agent,./pkg/trace/filters` → all tests pass (403 tests, 3 pre-existing skips unrelated to this change). - `git diff origin/main` reviewed line-by-line to confirm the legacy `*pb.Span` code paths (`normalize`, `Truncate`) were left untouched — on `pb.Span`, `Resource`/`Name` are struct fields and the existing `s.Resource`/`s.Name` usages there are correct as-is. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./cmd/serverless-init,./comp/core/log/impl-trace,./comp/process/gpusubscriber/impl,./pkg/config/remote/uptane,./pkg/privateactionrunner/bundles/helm,./cmd/process-agent/subcommands/status` → `0 issues.` (sanity check that no other consumer of `pkg/trace/log` regressed). - Added a `fixes:` release note via `reno new trace-log-printf-format-fixes`. ### Additional Notes ### Why not `DebugString()` `*idx.InternalSpan` does have a `DebugString()` helper, and it would satisfy the verb — but it dumps every span attribute. Attributes are unbounded in size and can carry request data (URLs, DB statements, custom tags), which makes them unsuitable for a value interpolated into a log line that fires once per malformed span. Both sites therefore log the identifying fields explicitly instead. `DebugString()` remains available for interactive debugging.

signals.title: [Backport 7.83.x] [CWS] Fix: handle activity dump endpoint host that already embeds a port
signals.text: Backport of #54774 to `7.83.x`. ### What was broken in 7.83 This is a **bug fix**. CWS activity dump uploads to dual-shipped `additional_endpoints` whose `host` already includes a port (e.g. `cws-intake.datadoghq.com.:443`) fail. `GetEndpointURL` appended the port a second time, producing a malformed `[host:port]:port` authority that failed URL parsing, so every upload to that endpoint failed with an `invalid port` error. In prod, CWS activity dumps were failing to reach the secondary (dual-ship) endpoint. ### Fix The host is now split before joining, so an embedded port is honored instead of duplicated. An explicitly configured port still wins, and bare IPv6 literals are untouched. ### Automated testing Test coverage is included in this backport (`pkg/security/utils/endpoint_test.go`), reproducing the exact prod host and asserting the resulting URL is accepted by `http.NewRequest` — the call that previously failed. Additional cases cover explicit-port precedence and IPv6 with an embedded port. ### Cherry-pick Cherry-picked cleanly (no conflicts) from `d4251bf9b58f48d1c28070dd662a1ef6d001936f`. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signals.title: NDM Agent Workload Balancing: gate check execution on group membership
signals.text: > **Note:** This PR was created by Claude. Third PR in the NDM Agent Workload Balancing sequence (after #54853 and #54993). Stacked on the `comp/workloadbalancing` component skeleton from #54993. ## What this does - Adds `WorkloadBalancingGroupID() string` to the `Check` interface and implements it across every implementer: `CheckBase` (default `""`), `StubCheck`, `stats.StatsCheck`, `PythonCheck`, the sharedlibrary `Check`, `APMCheck`, `ProcessAgentCheck`, and `middleware.CheckWrapper`. - Adds SNMP's new instance-level `agent_workload_balancing_group` field, including the `Copy()` fix so devices derived via `CopyWithNewIP` in subnet-discovery mode retain their group assignment instead of silently losing it. - Adds the gating branch in `pkg/collector/worker/worker.go`: a check with a non-empty workload balancing group runs only if `workloadBalancing.IsGroupActive(group)`; a check with no group keeps the existing HA-leader gating behavior unchanged. - Threads a `workloadbalancing.Component` dependency through `collector.go` -> `runner.go` -> `worker.go`, mirroring the existing `haAgent` wiring. ## Testing - `TestWorker_WorkloadBalancingGating` in `worker_test.go`: group active runs, group inactive skips, no group is unaffected by workload balancing gating. - SNMP config tests cover `agent_workload_balancing_group` YAML parsing, `Copy()`, and a discovery-mode case asserting `CopyWithNewIP` retains the group. - Verified clean `go build`/`go vet`/`go test` under default, `-tags test`, and `-tags python` for every touched package. The `-tags python` pass matters here since `PythonCheck` implements `Check` independently and a missed method there is exactly what caused a P1 build break on an earlier related PR (#54656). ## Deviation from the implementation plan The plan called for documenting `agent_workload_balancing_group` in `pkg/config/schema/yaml/core_schema.yaml`, "alongside wherever SNMP's other instance-level keys are documented." I checked and that file only covers `datadog.yaml`-level agent config; none of SNMP's existing instance-level keys (`community_string`, `ip_address`, etc.) appear there. There's no per-integration-instance schema doc location in this repo to add this field to, so I did not add an entry.

signals.title: fix(logonduration): make the boot_timeline offset axis monotone
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the `boot_timeline` axis monotone, so a milestone can no longer render ahead of one that happened before it. `bootOffsetFunc` collapsed the login-screen wait in a **single step**: `ts >= SessionLogon` was pulled left by the whole `SessionLogon - LoginUIDone` gap, everything else kept its raw offset. A step function is not order-preserving, and since the collapse maps `SessionLogon` onto `LoginUIDone`'s raw offset, the payload carried two clocks on one origin — an in-gap milestone at *how deep into the wait it started*, a post-logon one at *how long after logon it happened*. Nothing forces the first to be smaller. On the Aug 17 boot `computer_group_policy` lands at 10807 while `user_group_policy`, 25.7 s later in wall clock, lands at 8839. The premise the collapse rests on is false: that window is not idle. Machine Group Policy runs in it on all four traces we have, real and synthetic. **Fix:** elide only the sub-intervals of `[LoginUIDone, SessionLogon)` that no observed milestone covers. `offset(ts) = (ts - BootStart) - (elided time elapsed by ts)`. The derivative is 1 outside those stretches and 0 inside, so it is monotone by construction, and no milestone span can be elided because elision only happens where nothing was observed and a span *is* an observation. Nothing is truncated — an interval running past `SessionLogon` has no idle behind it to remove, so the overlap survives. It degrades to today's numbers when the region really is empty, and the timeline lengthens by exactly the busy time previously erased: +3483 ms on Aug 17, +49 ms on Aug 4, each the machine pass duration. The milestone candidate list moves into `timelineCandidates`, consumed by both the renderer and the busy-interval builder, so a milestone can never be rendered from an interval the axis did not know about. `group_policy_details` is fixed by the same change with no edit to `grouppolicy.go` — `finalize` already calls `bootOffsetFunc` for every CSE offset, so the child inversion clears with the parent. `durations` and `total_boot_duration_ms` are raw pairwise measurements and do not move. ### Motivation `boot_timeline` is a rendering axis; consumers read left-to-right as chronological. On a domain-joined machine it silently violated that on most boots, and `group_policy_details` now hangs off those milestones, so a wrong parent offset drags a child tree with it. The defect arrived with #50027 (`9b2dab34afc`), which introduced the login-screen gap collapse. It has never had a WINA ticket — worth filing before merge, since this moves a shipped number. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logonduration/impl` — **160 passing, 0 failing**. `dda inv linter.go` — 0 issues. The primary guard is a property test, `TestBootTimelineOffsetsAreMonotone`: sorted by wall-clock `Timestamp`, `OffsetMs` must be non-decreasing. Stronger than fixed expectations, holds for any input, and **fails on the shipped code** against the exact numbers the old test asserted. Runs over `fullBootTimeline` and all four new fixtures. `TestCSEOffsetsShareTheBootTimelineAxis` passes **unmodified** — its region has no busy interval, so it is elided whole. That it still passes is the evidence the change is confined to in-region activity. Four new cases in `TestBuildTimelineMilestones`, plus updated "full timeline" offsets (elided 2000 + 9000, not the full 19000): - **pass straddles `SessionLogon`** — the case that proves nothing is truncated: `8746..37275` against `logon_duration` at `34424..45097`, overlapping by exactly the 2851 ms the pass ran past logon - **pass absent** — full region elided, offsets identical to today - **`MachineGPEnd` absent** — pass has no span, region elided whole, point clamps to region start - **pass reaching in from before `LoginUIDone`** — only the idle after it is elided, bar keeps its full width New `TestCSEOffsetsKeepPassesInOrderAcrossTheLoginScreen` covers the reported shape the existing suite misses: a computer pass *inside* the region with CSEs alongside a user pass after logon, asserting each invocation nests in its parent and that the whole computer scope precedes the user scope. One expectation changed outside the plan: `TestCollector_FullBootSequence` asserted a CSE at 14000; it starts at boot+14s with 2000 ms elided ahead of it, so it is now 12000, still nested in its parent at `10000..18000`. **Not done:** the analyzer has not been re-run over the WINA-2940 boot ETL against this diff. The Aug 4 / Aug 17 figures come from the investigation that produced the change, not from executing this code on a capture. ### Additional Notes **`impl_darwin.go` is deliberately left on the single-step pattern.** The fix is a provable no-op there — its only candidates are `boot_duration`, `login_window_ready` (a point at the region start) and `logon_duration`, so nothing can land inside the region and it is elided whole either way. **CSE invocations are deliberately not in the busy list.** They live inside their pass, so they add nothing while it is present, and wiring `gpAccumulator` into the offset function would invert the current dependency. Follow-up for the case where an 8000 is missing and the pass has no span but its CSEs do. **Limit:** the rule does not establish the region is idle, only that nothing was observed there. Uninstrumented machine work at the login screen is still elided as think-time — that assumption is the feature's, unchanged since #50027. What this removes is the assumption erasing intervals we *did* observe. Left for their own PRs: `LoginUIDone` pair selection, `boot_timeline` array ordering (emitted in candidate order, never sorted — now a one-line change with no correctness question attached), unpaired pass endpoints, and WINA-3011 truncation. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [NETPATH-1118] Add baseline dynamic tests for CNM
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds opt-in baseline Dynamic Tests for Cloud Network Monitoring. Baseline mode observes eligible CNM traffic over a bounded window, selects up to five representative high-volume paths per Agent, and runs each winner once. #### Product contract - Baseline is a best-effort, automatically curated preview of Network Path. It does not guarantee coverage for a particular connection or destination. - The budget is per Agent: each completed window produces at most five baseline test runs. - Baseline favors stable, important traffic in v1. Diversity, rotation, and diagnostic-signal prioritization are intentionally deferred. - Standard connection-monitoring Dynamic Tests take precedence when enabled. #### Window lifecycle - The first window after baseline starts is five minutes to reduce time to first value. - Later windows are one hour. This cadence is intentionally separate from `network_path.collector.pathtest_interval`, which continues to control recurring Network Path tests. - Candidate ranking is updated continuously as CNM snapshots arrive. Admission is intentionally streaming: a periodic flush may split a concurrently processed snapshot across adjacent windows. This is a known and accepted limitation. - At each boundary, the final winners are submitted once and selection state is reset for the next window. #### Selection - Eligibility and filtering remain upstream. Baseline consumes already-admitted paths without depending on whether built-in, local, or Remote Configuration filtering admitted them. - Observations use the collector's existing normalized path identity: origin, namespace, hostname or IP, effective port, protocol, and source container ID. - A path's score is cumulative sent plus received bytes observed during the window. - Selection uses a weighted Space-Saving heavy-hitter estimator with a fixed 32-candidate set, keeping memory bounded independently of connection count. - Stable path identity provides deterministic tie-breaking. #### Execution - Winners are one-shot baseline executions rather than recurring TTL-backed contexts. - Existing queues, workers, concurrency controls, and rate limits remain shared with other Network Path tests. - A queue drop, rate-limit rejection, or execution failure does not restore the slot, promote another candidate, or trigger catch-up work. - Successful results carry `dynamic_test_profile: "baseline"`. ### Motivation Selecting paths independently from each CNM snapshot can accumulate recurring contexts and produce unstable coverage. Windowed heavy-hitter selection gives baseline a predictable contract: observe traffic over a meaningful period, choose up to five stable high-volume paths, and run each once. ### Test coverage requirements Comprehensive coverage is an acceptance requirement for this change. Tests must cover: - cumulative sent-plus-received byte ranking across multiple snapshots and repeated paths; - the five-minute bootstrap window, subsequent hourly windows, streaming boundary rollover, the accepted adjacent-window snapshot split, reset behavior, partial sets, and empty windows; - bounded candidate memory, heavy-hitter retention, deterministic ties, and overflow-safe accumulation; - the fixed baseline cadence, independence from `pathtest_interval`, and Standard Dynamic Tests precedence; - at-most-five one-shot submissions, including no replacement or retry after input-queue pressure or rate limiting; - preservation of filtering/Remote Configuration provenance and baseline payload attribution; - byte propagation from both CNM connection producers; - race safety for selector and store lifecycle changes; - a packaged-Agent E2E path through CNM traffic, system-probe traceroute, payload encoding, and fakeintake delivery. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/common:common_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test //comp/rdnsquerier/impl:impl_test //pkg/config/setup:setup_test //pkg/networkpath/payload:payload_test` - `bazel test --config=gorace //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test` - `bazel coverage //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test --combined_report=lcov` (100% line coverage for `baseline.go`; 97.5% for `pathteststore.go`) - `bazel build //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/dynamic-tests:dynamic-tests_test` The live AWS E2E has not yet been run. A passing packaged-Agent E2E is required before merge; its test binary compiles and CI wiring runs the netpath E2E job for the affected implementation paths. Local `dda inv` lint/test commands could not start because the internal Go toolchain mirror was not resolvable. Bazel validation above completed successfully. ### Additional Notes - Baseline uses a fixed five-test hourly budget, separate from `pathtest_interval`, so preview volume stays predictable without changing standard or NetFlow cadence. - The two connection-adapter paths are included in the netpath E2E change rules so byte-propagation changes continue to exercise this coverage. - This PR targets `main` directly and is not stacked on #54938.

signals.title: Make schema codegen emit uniform line endings
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Write the generated `pkg/config/setup` files through a `_write_uniform_lines` helper that opens with `newline="\n"`. Drop the trailing `out.append("")` from `gen_delegated_auth_map` and `gen_generate_const`: it only existed so a join separator would produce the final newline, and it forced the two write sites to disagree on whether to append one. ### Motivation `lint_windows-x64` has failed on all nightly main pipelines after #54160 moved the codegen into the lint path and stopped tracking its outputs ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1939819648)): ``` Linter failures: pkg\config\setup\all_settings.go:1:1: File is not properly formatted (gofmt) // Unless explicitly stated otherwise all files in this repository are licensed ^ pkg\config\setup\constants\generated.go:1:1: File is not properly formatted (gofmt) // Unless explicitly stated otherwise all files in this repository are licensed ^ pkg\config\setup\generated.go:1:1: File is not properly formatted (gofmt) // Unless explicitly stated otherwise all files in this repository are licensed ^ pkg\config\setup\system_probe_settings.go:1:1: File is not properly formatted (gofmt) // Unless explicitly stated otherwise all files in this repository are licensed ^ 4 issues: * gofmt: 4 Go linter result is 1 go linter failed 1 ``` Python text mode translates `\n` to `os.linesep`, so on Windows the freshly generated files land as CRLF and `gofmt` rejects them, whereas a checkout honors the `eol=lf` `.gitattributes`. Only nightly, deploy, tag and release pipelines run the job (`.on_native_os_linters`), so no pull request surfaced it. ### Describe how you validated your changes Ran `dda inv schema.codegen` on Linux and on Windows: both now produce the same md5 for all four files, with no CR and `gofmt` clean. `bazel build //pkg/config/setup:codegen_settings` yields outputs identical to the source tree. `bazel test //pkg/config/setup/...` and the 134 `tasks/unit_tests/schema_*_tests.py` cases pass.

signals.title: [datasecurity] resolve autodiscovery configs before matching postgres scan connections
signals.text: ## What - `resolvePostgresConnection` now reads `GetAllConfigs()` (resolved configs) instead of `GetUnresolvedConfigs()`, so autodiscovery template variables (`%%...%%`) are substituted before matching. - Adds `GetAllConfigs()` to the autodiscovery `Component` interface (+ noop impl). ## Why Postgres checks configured through autodiscovery annotations (`ad.datadoghq.com/postgres.checks`) use template variables that are only substituted once a service is matched. The scan-task resolver previously read *unresolved* configs, so a templated instance such as: ```yaml instances: - host: "%%host%%" port: 5432 dbm: true ``` could never match a scan-task entity, whose `database_host_name` is the concrete resolved host. And even if it did, the resulting connection would target `host: "%%host%%"`, which is not connectable. Reading the resolved config fixes both: the host is concrete and matchable. ## Why Backport to 7.83.x is justified - Tested the agent on my local machine and everything works as expected when using static Postgres check configs. - Data Security is a new product that is not enabled anywhere yet, so the blast radius of this change is effectively zero as the provider is not started unless data_security.enabled is set to true (default is false) - The bug was spotted while testing with autodiscovery-generated Postgres check configs. Back-porting allows support of autodiscovery-generated Postgres check configs in the upcoming 7.83.0 release.

signals.title: fix(e2e): flush fakeintake between flare suite tests (FLREM-153)
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `BeforeTest` override to `baseFlareSuite` (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/flare_common_test.go`) that flushes the fakeintake before each test, following the "one fakeintake per suite" convention documented in `test/new-e2e/AGENTS.md`. ### Motivation In e2e tests each test suite has its own fakeintake. Any test within a test suite uses the same fakeintake instance. `BeforeTest` fakeintake flush ensures that a test starts with an empty fakeintake, with no flares. `TestFlareDefaultFiles` has been flaking with `"Could not find diagnose.log file in flare archive"` (tracked in [FLREM-153](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FLREM-153)). The suite never reset the fakeintake between tests, so `GetLatestFlare()` — which just returns `payloads[len(payloads)-1]` — could pick up a flare left over from a previous test, or from the framework's post-failure diagnose-flare upload, instead of the one just requested by the current test. FLREM-153 also covers a second, unrelated flake (`TestLocalFlareDefaultFiles` hitting `context deadline exceeded` on the flare POST, due to the agent's hardcoded 60s HTTP client timeout combined with infra slowness). That one isn't addressed here — see the ticket comment for details. ### Describe how you validated your changes Traced the mechanics through `test/e2e-framework/testing/e2e/suite.go` (`BaseSuite.BeforeTest`/`AfterTest`/`IsDevMode`), `test/e2e-framework/testing/environments/host.go` (post-failure diagnose flare upload), and `test/fakeintake/client/client.go` (`FlushServerAndResetAggregators`, `GetLatestFlare`) to confirm the fix addresses the root cause and matches the identical pattern already used by ~10-15 other suites in this tree. ### Additional Notes [FLREM-153]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FLREM-153?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

Skip `test2json` and UTOF where their `bazel run` cannot match the test invocation, which is only the coverage job: its tests are a **subset** of `bazel:test:linux-amd64`, still reporting them, while its JUnit tar needs no Bazel and its coverage profile only `bazel info`, which analyzes nothing. Guard the remaining `bazel run` with `--noallow_analysis_cache_discard`, turning a future divergence into a failure of the job that introduces it, rather than a warning nobody reads until a monitor fires hours later on `main` pipelines. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv bazel.process-test-results --result-json=` runs no Bazel and still packages JUnit, while a non-empty one keeps converting logs. With the server left in the coverage configuration, the guarded command exits 2 on "analysis cache would have been discarded", and stays silent after `bazel test --config=gorace`. ### Additional Notes The guard is safe for the four `bazel:test:*` jobs: `INSTALL_DIR` and `AGENT_FLAVOR` are set by packaging jobs only, so `omnibazel_flags` injects nothing there, and neither monitor has reported a flip in those jobs since #54963.

signals.title: Convert linux_bpf to linux && bpf build tags
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Bazel requires a hint to understand whether a certain package is OS specific or not. One of the ways to do that is to use platform build tags like `linux`, `windows`, etc. In our case `linux_bpf` was de facto a platform constraint, but Bazel and Gazelle, a tool we use to automatically manage BUILD files, were not aware of that, so certain Linux only libraries were becoming unconditional dependencies for all the platforms. That was leading to failed builds and test executions. So, the simplest way out of this was to rename `linux_bpf` into `bpf` and add `linux` tag everywhere to have `linux && bpf`. ### Motivation First, it is technically more correct to rely more on standard go build tags. Second, this paves us the way to get rid of `bpf` tag in the near future. ### Additional Notes **Go Package Import Differences** is a false positive. Change in build tags led to a change in baseline being pretty much empty for the new layout. There are no changes in the imports

signals.title: Convert Bazel test logs to test2json in-graph via aspect
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Converts each Bazel `test.log` to test2json **during** `bazel test`, via an aspect on `TestRunner` actions, instead of shelling out to a converter afterwards. `tasks/bazel.py` then concatenates the resulting fragments. It already parsed the BEP to collect `test.xml` for JUnit, so fragment locations are picked up in that same pass — there is one BEP parser, and `process-test-results` no longer invokes Bazel at all. ### Motivation The previous flow ran `bazel run //bazel/tools/testlogs_to_json` in `after_script` with a hand-maintained label/log manifest. Conversion is naturally per-test work, so it belongs in the graph where it is cached and parallelised alongside the tests. ### Design notes **Fragment discovery comes from the BEP, not from filenames.** The aspect publishes a `test2json` output group; `targetCompleted` events carry that group, and its `fileSets` resolve through `namedSet` events to concrete file URIs. Nothing re-derives the aspect's naming scheme, so there is no filename contract between Starlark and Python. Outputs still in the remote cache report `bytestream://` rather than `file://`, so resolution falls back to the exec-root-relative path the BEP reports alongside. **Merging is not a Bazel action.** An earlier iteration expressed it as one, which was unsound: the rule declared only the BEP as an input and discovered fragments by globbing `bazel-out` at execution time, so nothing ordered it after the fragments, its cache key ignored their contents, and it required `no-sandbox` to run. After the aspect, aggregation is plain byte concatenation of newline-terminated JSONL, which does not warrant an action. **No post-test Bazel invocation.** This sidesteps configuration parity. The merge runs in `after_script`, where matching the test invocation's configuration would have meant threading per-job flag sets through CI — including a meaningless `--collect_code_coverage` for the coverage job, since `bazel coverage` implies it and it is configuration-affecting. **The Bazel label, not the Go import path, is the test2json package.** `dd_agent_go_test` emits several configured `go_test` targets for one Go package under different build-tag sets; collapsing them to one import path makes UTOF report distinct runs as retries of each other. ### Configuration `--config=test2json` enables the aspect and requests its output group. Bazel's `coverage` command inherits `test` options, so the `test:` lines cover both. No `--remote_download_regex` is needed: `--output_groups=+test2json` makes fragments top-level outputs, which `--remote_download_outputs=toplevel` already downloads. ### Possible drawbacks / Trade-offs Conversion is now on the critical path of the test invocation rather than in `after_script`, adding one small action per test target. In exchange those actions are cached and shared, so re-runs with cache hits do no conversion work at all. ### Describe how you validated your changes Local runs on macOS arm64, comparing against the previous manifest-based converter as the baseline: - **Output equivalence** — semantically identical to the manifest converter on the same BEP (104 events; the only differences across runs are wall-clock durations embedded in `--- PASS:` text). - **Failing tests** — a deliberately failing target still publishes its `test2json` group, and its `fail` events reach the merged output. Tests execute exactly once; making the aspect depend on `test.log` does not cause double-runs. - **Remote cache** — after `bazel clean`, with 108 remote cache hits and 9 of 10 tests served from cache, all 10 fragments materialised under `--remote_download_outputs=toplevel`. This rules out local action-cache re-materialisation masking the result. - **Multiple actions per target** — under `--runs_per_test=2`, two targets produced 4 uniquely named fragments, all reaching the merged output, with UTOF reporting them as retries. - **`bazel coverage`** — publishes the `test2json` group with only the `test:` config lines present. - **Failure path** — a BEP from a run without the aspect produces an actionable error rather than an empty result. - Unit tests for the aspect converter; `buildifier --lint=warn`, `gofmt` and `ruff` clean. CI will exercise the five reporting jobs (linux amd64/arm64, macOS amd64/arm64, coverage) on real `//...` invocations.

signals.title: [CWS] Buffer security profile v2 metrics in atomics
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Moves the remaining inline `statsdClient` **counter** emissions in `ManagerV2` (`pkg/security/security_profile/manager_v2.go`) onto the existing accumulate-in-atomics + flush-once-in-`SendStats()` pattern already used by the sample-refresh, event-filtering, insertion-error and per-`(source, event_type)` counters. Converted: | Metric | Was emitted from | Now | |---|---|---| | `security_profile_v2.tag_resolution.events_dropped` | `purgeStalePendingEvents` | `tagResolutionEventsDropped` atomic | | `security_profile_v2.tag_resolution.cgroups_expired` | `purgeStalePendingEvents` | `tagResolutionCgroupsExpired` atomic | | `security_profile_v2.cleanup.profiles_removed` | `cleanupPendingProfiles` | `cleanupProfilesRemoved` atomic | | `security_profile_v2.eviction.runs` | `evictUnusedNodes` | `evictionRuns` atomic | | `security_profile_v2.eviction.nodes_evicted_per_profile` | `evictUnusedNodes` | `evictionNodesEvicted` atomic | | `security_profile_v2.size_in_bytes` + `security_profile_v2.persisted_profiles` (tagged) | `sendPersistenceMetrics` | precomputed `persistenceMetrics` map keyed by `(format, storage_type, compression)` | The tagged persistence counters follow the `eventMetrics`/`initEventMetrics` precedent: a pre-populated map of atomic buckets with precomputed tag slices, so there's no locking or per-emit allocation on the persist path. The `security_profile_v2.tag_resolution.latency` distribution is intentionally left inline, since a distribution can't collapse into a single counter without losing the histogram. ## Motivation Keep metric reporting off the hot / ticker paths and consolidate emission in `SendStats()`, consistent with the rest of the manager. ## Describe how you validated your changes - `go build ./pkg/security/security_profile/` - `go vet ./pkg/security/security_profile/` All converted counters are untagged (or share the same tag set), so summing the accumulated values and emitting once per cycle is equivalent to the previous per-call emissions. ## Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs Per-profile eviction and per-persist emissions are now aggregated per `SendStats` cycle rather than emitted individually; since they share identical tags this does not change the aggregated series. ## Additional Notes Draft for review. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signals.title: feat(ssi): last-TRUE-wins SSI matching
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Unify SSI matching on a single last-TRUE-wins matcher: - **Static targets** (Helm / Operator / `datadog.yaml`) are reversed at construction so config first-wins is preserved. - **RC policies** keep wire order (catch-all first, exceptions after) and are last-TRUE-wins as-is. - Evaluation is static first, then RC, then SSI inject-all only when both are absent. A matched deny does not fall through. ``` SSI | static targets | RC | Decision off | — | none | nothing off | — | policies | last matching policy, else nothing on | none | none | everything on | none | policies | last matching policy, else nothing on | present | none | first (as in the yaml) matching target, else nothing on | present | policies | first (as in the yaml) matching target, else last matching policy, else nothing ``` Stacked on #55057. ### Motivation RC is already last-wins on the wire. Using the same matcher for static targets (by reversing them) avoids two matching modes. Static targeting is evaluated before RC so a remote deny cannot override an explicit local target. ### Describe how you validated your changes - [x] Unit tests: `./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/autoinstrumentation` - [ ] E2E `TestSSISuite/TestRemoteConfig` (HelmTargetWinsOverRemoteDeny, LastMatchingRemotePolicyWins) ### Additional Notes `HelmTargetWinsOverRemoteDeny` now expects the helm python workload to **keep** SSI when an RC deny matches `targeted-namespace`. That inverts the parent PR, where remote-before-local made the deny win.

signals.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  [datasecurity] resolve autodiscovery configs before matching postgres scan connections
signals.text: Backport bd1766d0c0b2273d893eb042499c9968c79c61a4 from #55078. ___ ## What - `resolvePostgresConnection` now reads `GetAllConfigs()` (resolved configs) instead of `GetUnresolvedConfigs()`, so autodiscovery template variables (`%%...%%`) are substituted before matching. - Adds `GetAllConfigs()` to the autodiscovery `Component` interface (+ noop impl). ## Why Postgres checks configured through autodiscovery annotations (`ad.datadoghq.com/postgres.checks`) use template variables that are only substituted once a service is matched. The scan-task resolver previously read *unresolved* configs, so a templated instance such as: ```yaml instances: - host: "%%host%%" port: 5432 dbm: true ``` could never match a scan-task entity, whose `database_host_name` is the concrete resolved host. And even if it did, the resulting connection would target `host: "%%host%%"`, which is not connectable. Reading the resolved config fixes both: the host is concrete and matchable. ## Why Backport to 7.83.x is justified - Tested the agent on my local machine and everything works as expected when using static Postgres check configs. - Data Security is a new product that is not enabled anywhere yet, so the blast radius of this change is effectively zero as the provider is not started unless data_security.enabled is set to true (default is false) - The bug was spotted while testing with autodiscovery-generated Postgres check configs. Back-porting allows support of autodiscovery-generated Postgres check configs in the upcoming 7.83.0 release.

signals.title: ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors, by giving apt real per-request failover: - Rewrites the deb822 `URIs:` fields in `ubuntu.sources` to an ordered multi-URI list (`us-west-2`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `mirror.leaseweb.net`) so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - Drops `us-east-1` (the chronically-slow mirror in the timeout logs). - `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout so a slow mirror becomes a fast error that triggers failover. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs, across many branches). The build spent its whole wall-clock in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror. A first attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** fix it: apt's `mirror` method sticks to one mirror per invocation and only fails over when it's fully unreachable, so a slow-but-reachable `us-east-1` kept timing out and `Acquire::Retries` retried the same URI to the job timeout. This PR switches to explicit ordered `URIs:` for genuine per-request failover. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs isolated mirror throughput as the only variable (successful same-commit runs finished in 16-21m). - Validated the `sed` `URIs:` rewrite against the default noble `ubuntu.sources`. - CI will exercise the real build here. ### Additional Notes The same fix is applied to the other CI Dockerfiles in #55119. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [7.82.x] ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signals.text: Backport of #55108 to `7.82.x`. ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors: - Adds `Acquire::Retries` + a 15s `Acquire` timeout so a stalled request is dropped and retried against the next mirror. - Lists mirrors as peers (drops the `priority:1` pin) and adds `us-west-2` and `mirror.leaseweb.net`, so apt load-balances and fails over across them. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs). The full 30-40m was spent in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror; the old `priority:1` pin only failed over when that mirror was fully unreachable, not when merely slow. ### Describe how you validated your changes Clean cherry-pick of the `main` commit. CI will exercise the real build here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
