signals.title: sbom: default runtime usage properties only on OS packages
signals.text: The core-agent enrichment merge walks every component of an image SBOM and copies the runtime usage properties onto the ones the system-probe report covers, then defaults LastSeenRunning to "0" and HasSetSuidBit and RunningAsRoot to "false" on all the rest. The runtime scanner reads the dpkg, rpm and apk databases only, so a language package, the image's operating-system component and Trivy's per-lockfile application components can never be reported. They were being defaulted all the same, which states that the component was watched and never seen running when in truth it was never in scope. Default the three properties only for a component the report carried or whose purl marks it an OS package. Everything else keeps them absent, which is what a consumer needs in order to tell "watched, not in use" from "unknown". Trivy maps every OS family to the deb, rpm and apk purl types, so the prefix is enough to decide, and the same three prefixes already serve this purpose in the SBOM e2e tests. Language packages only appear when sbom.container_image.analyzers includes "languages", but the operating-system component is in every image SBOM, so the new e2e phase is exercised on every enriched image the fake intake holds.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: sbom: key the runtime enrichment dedup on bom-ref
signals.text: The core-agent enrichment merge rebuilds the component list of the image SBOM it annotates, dropping any component whose name and normalised version it has already emitted. That treats a name and a version as an identity, and they are not one: Trivy reports one component per install location, so a library version pinned by two lockfiles appears once per lockfile, with a bom-ref of its own for each. The merge kept the first and dropped the rest, so the payload lost real components, and the dependency graph, which the merge carries over untouched, went on referencing the ones that were gone. Deduplicate on the bom-ref instead, which is what identifies a component in CycloneDX, and emit every component that has none, since folding those together on any other key is the same mistake. The guard is still worth keeping: it was added against a stored SBOM holding one component twice, and a byte-for-byte duplicate shares its bom-ref, so that case still collapses. Duplicate name and version pairs come from the language ecosystems, so this only shows up when sbom.container_image.analyzers includes "languages".

signals.title: sbom: run the SBOM e2e job on core-agent collector changes
signals.text: The runtime usage properties an SBOM payload carries are produced by the merge in comp/core/workloadmeta/collectors/internal/remote/sbomcollector, and TestSBOMPackageInUseKubeadmSuite is what exercises that merge end to end. The rule that triggers new-e2e-sbom lists the system-probe resolver and the test tree but not the collector, so a change confined to it reaches the suite only if someone starts the job by hand. Add the collector to the rule.

signals.title: fix(installer): secure Windows config rollback
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes Windows Fleet Automation config experiment rollback so it: - copies YAML ACLs from a securely created backup directory - removes only allowlisted Fleet-managed YAML that is absent from the backup - preserves unmanaged files and directories under `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` - rejects incomplete YAML copies and legacy symlink mismatches before deleting the backup - uses slash-aware allowlist matching and root-confined deletion to avoid over-deleting YAML or following swapped junctions - reconciles legacy v2 managed symlinks (`stable` / `experiment`) before robocopy and verifies they are restored Adds selective-cleanup, copy-validation, legacy-link, and Windows ACL/unmanaged-file regression tests, plus a release note. ### Motivation Addresses [WINA-2053](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2053) and the failure observed in [SPFA-180](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SPFA-180). The current `robocopy /MIR /SL ... *.yaml` rollback can purge destination content and recreates deleted files without their original ACLs. Adding `/SEC` by itself was previously unsafe because an unprivileged user could pre-create the destination between deletion and ACL repair while retaining an open handle. The current implementation now securely creates the experiment root with the stable root's security descriptor before copying, and never removes the stable root before restore. This change uses that prerequisite, removes `/MIR`, scopes rollback deletion in Go to managed YAML only, and treats robocopy mismatch exit codes 4-7 as rollback failure. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/config --no-cache` (64 passed) - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/config --only-modified-packages` - `bazelisk test //pkg/fleet/installer/config:config_test` - `bazelisk build //pkg/fleet/installer/config:config --platforms=@rules_go//go/toolchain:windows_amd64` - Pre-commit and pre-push hooks, including release-note validation Windows-only tests cover ACL restore, junction rejection, and v2 symlink rollback, including backups whose copied absolute `stable`/`experiment` links still point at the original tree (`robocopy /SL`). Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) [WINA-2053]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2053?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [SPFA-180]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SPFA-180?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: env: warn when a container socket exists but is not reachable
signals.text: Feature detection reports this with log.Infof, but it runs while the configuration is still loading, so the message is buffered and only filtered against the final log level once the logger is installed. On an Agent running at log_level warn it is discarded and never written anywhere. The condition deserves a warning. On Unix socket.IsAvailable calls a socket unreachable only when the dial fails with a permission error, so the Agent user cannot open it and container metrics, container image collection and container image vulnerability scanning are all silently disabled. Windows also counts a pipe that is merely busy, but a pipe the Agent cannot open in half a second is worth surfacing too. No test. A socket that exists and cannot be opened is not something a test can build while running as root, which is how CI runs.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: sbom: warn when container image scanning has no container runtime
signals.text: Container image SBOMs come from images that workloadmeta discovers through the container runtime. With no runtime the collectors stay disabled, no image entity is ever created, and the check reports itself healthy while emitting only the host SBOM. A customer spent a week on a correct configuration because nothing said the images were never found. Warn once at configuration time. The gate is sbom.container_image.enabled, which defaults to false, rather than container_image.enabled, which defaults to true and would warn on nearly every host without containers. The check is only scheduled when sbom.enabled is true, so setting sbom.container_image.enabled on its own stays as silent as before. Only Docker, containerd and CRI-O build image SBOMs, so the runtime test names those three rather than calling IsAnyContainerFeaturePresent. That helper also answers true for Kubernetes, ECS, Cloud Foundry and Podman, and a Kubernetes node whose runtime socket is not mounted is precisely the case this warning exists for.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: healthplatform: correct the docker permission issue impact
signals.text: The check that raises this issue detects an unreachable Docker socket, so the Agent cannot query the daemon at all and container metrics, container image collection and container image vulnerability scanning all go quiet. The impact named only the log tailing fallback, so an operator chasing missing images would read the issue and dismiss it. Worse, that fallback cannot happen. Socket tailing needs the very socket that is unreachable. Everything named is scoped to Docker. The check only proves that a default Docker socket exists and cannot be opened, not that Docker is the runtime in use, so a containerd or CRI-O node with a stale inaccessible socket keeps reporting all of it through its own collector. Only the impact text changes. Title, Description and the remediation still describe the log directory case that the logs producer raised before 058e777637d removed it, and the remediation ACLs "<socket>/containers", which helps nobody whose dd-agent user is not in the docker group. Correcting that means replacing the embedded scripts, so it is left for a separate change.

signals.title: ci: make apt mirror config resilient to slow mirrors across agent images
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes CI Docker builds resilient to slow public package mirrors, across every image in this repo that installs packages from a public host — each fitted to its own package system. **Ubuntu (apt) — multi-URI failover** (`agent`, `base-image`, `cluster-agent`, `otel-agent`, `ddot-ebpf`, podman e2e resource): apt's `mirror` method can't fail over off a *slow* mirror (only a fully-unreachable one), so instead of a mirrorlist we rewrite the deb822 `URIs:` fields in `ubuntu.sources` to an ordered multi-URI list. apt tries them in order and fails over on error. Drop `us-east-1` (chronically slow in every timeout log); order `us-west-2` → `archive.ubuntu.com` → `mirror.leaseweb.net`. `Retries "1"` + 10s timeout so a slow mirror becomes a fast error. **Debian (apt)** (`test/fakeintake`, golang base): rewrite `debian.sources` `URIs:` to Debian's AWS/CloudFront mirror `cdn-aws.deb.debian.org` first, `deb.debian.org` fallback, + Acquire timeout/Retries. (Debian has no EC2 archive mirror like Ubuntu; cdn-aws is its AWS-region CDN.) **Alpine (apk)** (`Dockerfiles/dogstatsd/alpine`, `test/fakeintake` deploy stage): list `dl-cdn` primary + `mirror.clarkson.edu` secondary (apk fails over in listed order), and add the global `apk --timeout` so a slow mirror fails fast. ### Motivation `docker_build_host_profiler_standalone_amd64` was timing out (~30m, across many branches incl. 7.83.x). Its `release` stage builds on `agent-base-image` (= `Dockerfiles/agent/Dockerfile`), whose `apt-get` stalled against a congested `us-east-1`. An earlier attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** stop it: job `1965243524` showed apt sticking to the slow `us-east-1` and retrying the same URI to the job timeout, even though `us-west-2` served ~90 packages in one second when apt picked it. The `mirror` method has no per-request failover on slowness — hence the switch to explicit ordered `URIs:`. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs pinpointed the stall inside the apt step of the agent-base-image release stage on a slow `us-east-1`, and showed `us-west-2` healthy. - Validated the Ubuntu and Debian `sed` `URIs:` rewrites against the default noble `ubuntu.sources` / trixie `debian.sources` (GNU sed semantics). - Confirmed `apk --timeout` is a valid global flag (must precede the subcommand). - CI will exercise the real builds here. ### Additional Notes Local dev-tooling Dockerfiles (`tools/gdb`, `tools/ebpf/*-agent-dev`) are excluded — they don't run under `CI=true` and aren't in any CI build path. `agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` is handled by #55108. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: fix(wlan): do not panic when wlanapi.dll is unavailable on Windows
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Stops the Windows `wlan` check from panicking when `wlanapi.dll` cannot be loaded. `wlanapi.dll` ships with the Windows `Wireless-Networking` feature, which is **not installed by default on Windows Server**. `windows.LazyProc.Call` panics (via `mustFind`) instead of returning an error when it cannot resolve the DLL, so the very first call in `getWlanHandle` blew up. `GetWiFiInfo` now loads the DLL before calling into it, and reports no active Wi-Fi interface (`phyMode: "None"` → WARNING status) when the load fails. A host with no WLAN stack has no Wi-Fi interface to report on, which is a normal server state rather than a collection failure. `LazyDLL.Load` already caches the module handle on success and guards itself with a mutex, so calling it per run costs a single atomic load once the library is present — no `sync.Once` needed, and wrapping it in one would additionally cache the *failure*, which `Load` deliberately does not. Loading per run also means a host that installs `Wireless-Networking` starts reporting on the next check tick with no Agent restart. ### Motivation Jira: [WINA-3050](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3050) Reported crash: the Agent process crashes on Windows Server when the `wlan` check is enabled and there is no Wi-Fi. Reproduced on a Windows Server 2022 VM with no `Wireless-Networking` feature installed (`wlanapi.dll` absent, `wlansvc` not registered), running Agent 7.82.1: ``` panic: The specified module could not be found. golang.org/x/sys/windows.(*LazyProc).mustFind(...) golang.org/x/sys@v0.47.0/windows/dll_windows.go:293 golang.org/x/sys/windows.(*LazyProc).Call(...) golang.org/x/sys@v0.47.0/windows/dll_windows.go:315 +0x59 .../wlan.getWlanHandle() wlan_windows.go:375 .../wlan.getFirstConnectedWlanInfo() wlan_windows.go:468 .../wlan.(*WLANCheck).GetWiFiInfo() wlan_windows.go:516 .../wlan.(*WLANCheck).Run() wlan.go:158 .../check.runCheck(...) command.go:674 ``` Two symptoms depending on the path: - **`agent check wlan`** — hard crash, full panic to stderr, non-zero exit (the CLI path has no recover). - **Long-running agent service** — survives thanks to the recover in `pkg/collector/worker`, but degrades permanently: the panic is recovered and re-logged every 15s, a MEDIUM health-platform issue stays open, and no `system.wlan.*` metrics are ever emitted. ``` ERROR | worker.go:232 | Recovered from panic in check wlan: The specified module could not be found. ERROR | check_logger.go:71 | check:wlan | Error running check: check panicked: ... INFO | Health platform: NEW issue from collector: Check 'wlan' Failed (ISSUE_SEVERITY_MEDIUM) ``` On an Agent older than #49763 (which added the worker recover, so roughly pre-7.75) the service itself would have died outright. Note the trigger is *no WLAN stack*, not *no Wi-Fi network*. A server with the feature installed but not associated to an AP already worked correctly. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Reproduced the original panic on the affected VM (Windows Server 2022, Agent 7.82.1), both via `agent check wlan` and in the running service log. - Added `wlan_windows_test.go` (`windows && test`): with the loader stubbed to fail, `GetWiFiInfo` does not panic and returns `phyMode: "None"` with no error. Deterministic on any runner, including ones that do have the DLL. - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/net/wlan` — 17 tests pass. - `GOOS=windows dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/net/wlan --build-tags=test` — 0 issues; verified the Windows-only test file is actually typechecked (temporarily injected a type error and confirmed the linter caught it). - `BUILD.bazel` regenerated with `bazel run //:gazelle`, then formatted with `bazel run //bazel/buildifier` (no changes produced). `bazel test //bazel/buildifier:test` passes, so the file is clean in both `diff` and `warn` lint mode. **Verified end-to-end on the affected host.** Installed this PR's pipeline MSI (`pipelines/A7/131968742`, `7.84.0-devel.git.310.3d4ea7b`, SHA256 verified after transfer) on the same Windows Server 2022 VM that reproduced the crash, with `wlanapi.dll` still absent and the same `wlan.d/conf.yaml` in place. | | Before (7.82.1) | After (3d4ea7b) | |---|---|---| | `agent check wlan` | `panic: The specified module could not be found.`, non-zero exit | `Instance ID: wlan [OK]`, **exit code 0** | | Service, per 15s run | 2 ERROR lines + MEDIUM health issue | `Running check...` → `Done running check`, no errors | | New recovered panics after restart | every run | **0** over 75s / 6 runs | | `system.wlan.*` metrics | none emitted | `system.wlan.status = 1` (warning), `reason:interface_inactive` | | Health platform | `Check 'wlan' Failed (ISSUE_SEVERITY_MEDIUM)` | no issue raised | Confirmed the new branch is what executes, rather than the check succeeding for some unrelated reason (`--log-level debug`): ``` DEBUG | (pkg/collector/corechecks/net/wlan/wlan_windows.go:527 in GetWiFiInfo) | Skipping Wi-Fi collection, wlanapi.dll is unavailable: The specified module could not be found. WARN | (pkg/collector/corechecks/net/wlan/wlan.go:179 in Run) | No active Wi-Fi interface detected: PHYMode is none. ``` Same underlying Windows error that used to be the panic, now a debug line and a WARNING status. ### Additional Notes The shipped `wlan.d/conf.yaml.default` carries the `_end_user_device` AD identifier, which normally keeps this check off servers; reproducing required a hand-written `wlan.d/conf.yaml`, which is presumably what the reporting host has. [WINA-3050]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3050?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: [CWS-6779] Implement the setns syscall
signals.text:
### What does this PR do? Adds a `setns` event to CWS: an eBPF hook on the `setns` syscall, a `setns` event in the event model wired through to SECL, a backend serializer, and functional test coverage. Fields exposed: | Field | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `setns.fd` | File descriptor of the namespace the thread requested to join | | `setns.nstype` | Requested namespace types — bitmask over the new `CLONE_NEW*` SECL constants (`0` = kernel infers the type from the fd) | | `setns.mntns` | MNTNS ID of the thread once the syscall returned | | `setns.netns` | NetNS ID of the thread once the syscall returned | | `setns.retval` | Return value (standard `SyscallEvent`) | Successful calls **and** `-EPERM`/`-EACCES` are reported (via the usual `IS_UNHANDLED_ERROR`), so denied attempts stay visible. ### Motivation CWS could already see namespace *creation* (`unshare_mntns`), but nothing fired when a thread *joined* an existing namespace. That is the primitive behind most container-escape and privilege-escalation chains: open `/proc/1/ns/net` (or any leaked nsfs fd), then `setns` into it. This gives the detection team signal to write rules against. A bare fd number is not rule-able on its own, so the event also resolves the namespace IDs the thread ends up in, which is what makes the escape detectable: ``` setns.nstype == CLONE_NEWNET && setns.netns == setns.mntns != ``` Those IDs come from extending `hook_switch_task_namespaces` — a hook that is already attached unconditionally and that `setns` necessarily goes through to commit its new `nsproxy`. Sequence: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as Thread (user space) participant K as Kernel participant E as eBPF (runtime-security) participant A as security-agent U->>K: setns(fd, nstype) K->>E: hook_setns — syscall entry E->>E: cache_syscall EVENT_SETNS {fd, nstype} K->>K: validate_nsset / commit_nsset K->>E: hook_switch_task_namespaces(task, new nsproxy) E->>E: read mnt_ns->inum / net_ns->inum
into the live EVENT_SETNS cache K->>E: hook_setns exit (or raw_syscalls:sys_exit tail call) E->>A: send_event EVENT_SETNS
{fd, nstype, mntns_id, netns_id, retval} A->>A: SECL evaluation over setns.* ``` Only mount and network are resolvable — `nsproxy_mnt_ns_offset` and `nsproxy_net_ns_offset` are the only `nsproxy` offsets available. Unresolved is reported as `0`. ### Describe how you validated your changes New `TestSetNS` (`pkg/security/tests/setns_test.go`) with four subtests, driven by a new `setns` command in `syscall_tester.c`. It is a C helper rather than Go on purpose: `setns` is per-thread, so calling it from the multi-threaded test binary would either fail (`CLONE_NEWNS` needs `fs->users == 1`) or strand a Go runtime thread in a foreign namespace. - `join-own-netns` / `join-own-mntns` — asserts `nstype`, `retval`, a valid `fd`, and that the reported ID equals the inode of `/proc/self/ns/{net,mnt}` - `infer-nstype` — `nstype == 0`; the requested type is reported as-is while the ID is still resolved - `netns-roundtrip` — holds a fd to the current netns, `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, then `setns` back. Asserts the reported netns is the **original** one and not the transient unshared one, which is what proves the ID is resolved per-event rather than read from a stale cache Each subtest also validates the serialized event against the new `setns.schema.json`. Run locally on a 6.x kernel (kprobe mode — this kernel forces the fentry fallback, so the fentry path is compile-verified here and covered functionally by KMT): | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `TestSetNS` | 4/4 pass | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/model` | 894 pass | | `bazel build //pkg/security/ebpf/...` | 20 targets; `sys_setns` + `handle_sys_setns_exit` present in both kprobe and fentry objects | | Regression check on namespace-adjacent tests | `TestPivotRoot`, `TestProcessContext`, `TestProcessSID`, `TestSetrlimitEvent`, `TestSocketEvent`, `TestBindEvent`, `TestConnectEvent*` all pass | | `golangci-lint` (`secl/model`, `serializers`, `probe`, `ebpf/probes`, `tests`) | 0 issues | | `validate-cws-generated-files` pre-push hook | Passed | Sample serialized event, captured from a live run: ```json "setns": { "fd": 3, "nstype": "CLONE_NEWNET", "mntns": 4026532592, "netns": 4026532595 } ``` ### Additional Notes **No release note**, intentionally — hence `changelog/no-changelog`. Worth a reviewer's opinion: this *is* user-facing (a new SECL event), so if you'd rather have it in the CHANGELOG, say so and I'll add a reno note and drop the label.
Design decisions worth a reviewer's eye - **`mntns`/`netns` are post-syscall values, not strictly "the namespace joined."** The kernel commits the whole `nsproxy`, so both are populated even for a `CLONE_NEWNET`-only call. The SECL docs are worded to say exactly that rather than overstate it. Filling both is strictly more informative than branching on the requested type — and for `nstype == 0` the type isn't known at entry anyway. - **`setns.fd` is `int`, not `int32`.** The accessor generator has no `setInt32FieldValue`, and no other exposed field uses `int32`. - **`nstype == 0` serializes as `"ANY"`.** The default bitmask stringer renders `""`, which reads as missing data; `0` is a documented, meaningful value for this syscall, so it got a name. - **eBPF only.** No ebpfless/ptracer wiring, matching how `setsid` and `pivot_root` shipped (`setrlimit` added ebpfless later in #44114). `TestSetNS` is deliberately absent from the ebpfless allowlist in `main_linux.go`, so it auto-skips there. - **No rate limiter.** `setns` is rare outside container runtimes and `nsenter`, unlike `setrlimit` which needed one. If QA on a busy node shows runtime chatter, a `pid_rate_limiter_allow` guard on the entry hook is the fix. - **Pre-existing wart, left alone:** `LastEventType` is still `PivotRootEventType` even though `setsid`/`nop`/`socket` come after it. It only bounds the `applyDefaultFilterPolicies` loop and mode `0` is `PolicyModeNoFilter`, so appending `setns` after it is harmless. Happy to fix separately.

signals.title: compliance/k8sconfig: fix kubelet defaults when --config is used
signals.text: Kubernetes keeps the historical command line default of a few kubelet flags to preserve the command line API, and drops them as soon as the kubelet is started with --config. The configuration file is then loaded with the KubeletConfiguration defaults instead, and only the flags that appear on the command line are applied on top of it. The loader applied the command line defaults in both cases. The two sets of defaults disagree on exactly the three settings the CIS Kubernetes benchmarks care about. A kubelet reading a configuration file that leaves them out runs with the read-only port disabled, anonymous authentication disabled and Webhook authorization, while the loader reported a read-only port on 10255, anonymous authentication enabled and an AlwaysAllow authorization mode. Neither OpenShift nor kubeadm write readOnlyPort into their rendered configuration, so their nodes failed "The kubelet read-only port should be disabled" with the port closed. The generator now carries the configuration file default next to the command line one for those three flags, and the loader picks between them depending on whether the component reads a configuration file at all. The payload version is bumped so that rules can tell the two apart. Updates CSPDE-1519.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: compliance/k8sconfig: do not report an unreadable file as empty
signals.text: The loader stats a configuration file, reads it, then parses whatever it got. A read that fails, typically a permission denied on a kubeconfig the Agent does not own, was recorded in the errors list and otherwise ignored. Parsing no bytes at all yields an empty configuration, which is indistinguishable from a file that is really empty, and nothing downstream consults the errors list. So an unreadable file quietly became a file holding nothing. detectManagedEnvironment falls back to the kubelet kubeconfig to recognize an EKS, GKE or AKS control plane when the node labels say nothing, and it walked the three empty maps of a manufactured kubeconfig to conclude that the node was unmanaged. Content that could not be read is now left out rather than parsed, so the detection is left with nothing to go on instead of invented evidence. It still reports such a node as unmanaged, because there is no resource type for a node we cannot identify, which is a separate matter. The ownership and permissions we did manage to stat are kept, which also fixes the benchmarks looking at them. They used to see a mode of zero for an unreadable kubelet configuration file and pass. Updates CSPDE-1519.

signals.title: fix(windows): don't lock out the domain agent user account on upgrade
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the Windows MSI set `dd-procmgr-service`'s start type to **disabled** when the Agent user password is not available, and back to **demand start** once it is available again. The condition is deliberately narrowed to **domain accounts**: | account type | `isDomainAccount` | `isServiceAccount` | password empty? | start type | |---|---|---|---|---| | domain user, password supplied or from LSA | true | false | no | `Manual` | | **domain user, no password anywhere** | **true** | **false** | **yes** | **`Disabled`** ← the bug | | local user, no password supplied | false | false | no (generated) | `Manual` | | gMSA | – | true | yes | `Manual` | | LocalSystem / LocalService / NetworkService | – | true | yes | `Manual` | Local accounts can never reach the disable path, because `ProcessDdAgentUserCredentials` generates a random 128-character password when none is supplied (`ProcessUserCustomActions.cs`), and gMSA plus the well-known accounts are already covered by `IsServiceAccount`. `IsDomainAccount` is only evaluated once the password is known to be missing, so **the common install path is unchanged**. ### Motivation Fixes IR-59268 (SEV-3). `dd-procmgr-service` moved from `LocalSystem` to `ddagentuser` in 7.82.0 and, unlike the earlier services that hit this same class of bug (security-agent, DDOT, PAR), it **runs by default**. On a manual MSI upgrade that does not re-provide `DDAGENTUSER_PASSWORD` and has no LSA secret — the case for hosts first installed with **7.65 or earlier**, since only 7.66+ began storing it: 1. `InstallServices` creates the service with a domain account and an **empty password**. 2. `ConfigureServiceUsers` sees no password and passes `null` to `SetCredentials`, which leaves the empty password in place. 3. The service fails to log on (Event 7000/7038, Security 4625 substatus `0xC000006A`). 4. Failure actions are `restart` ×3 with `RestartServiceDelayInSeconds = 60`, but **`ResetPeriodInDays = 0`** makes the SCM reset the failure counter immediately, so it applies the *first* action forever and never exhausts the three restarts. Hence Event 7031 reporting *"It has done this 1 time(s)"* on every iteration, and an **unbounded 60-second retry loop**. 5. Five failed logons **lock out the account in about 4 minutes**, unattended, on a single host — and because it is a domain account, the Agent then fails to start on **every host sharing it**. Three customers have reported it; one is uninstalling the Agent from their Windows fleet. Affected hosts already on 7.82.0–7.82.2 self-heal on upgrade, though the account still has to be unlocked once. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests** — new `CustomActions.Tests/Service/ProcmgrStartTypeTests.cs`, 8 cases: domain-without-password → `Disabled`; domain-with-password, **local-without-password**, gMSA and LocalSystem → `Manual`; `ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` swallowed; any other failure propagates; and no other service's start type is touched. **E2E, domain** — new `testUpgradeWithoutStoredPasswordSuite` in `tests/windows/domain-test` installs **7.65.2-1** with a domain account and password, upgrades **without** a password, then asserts: - `dd-procmgr-service` start type is `SERVICE_DISABLED` - the account never appears in `Search-ADAccount -LockedOut` over a 6-minute window (the real lockout took ~4) - no System 7000/7031/7038 or Security 4625 events mentioning the service or user in that window - the core Agent is healthy and payloads reach the fakeintake - **positive control:** re-installing *with* the password restores `SERVICE_DEMAND_START` and the service starts The existing `testUpgradeSuite` does not catch this, because it installs last stable (7.82.x), which already stores the LSA secret. **E2E, non-domain** — one assertion added to `install-test`'s `TestUpgrade`, which is the exact local-account analogue (default local `ddagentuser`, upgraded without a password), asserting the service **stays enabled**. Verified locally: `7.65.2-1` is present for `x86_64` in the live `installers_v2.json`; both E2E packages pass `gofmt` and `go vet`; release note passes `linter.rst-releasenotes` and `linter.releasenote-unique-ids`. **Not yet validated — please note before reviewing:** - The C# is **not compile-verified locally** (no `dotnet`/`msbuild`/`mono` available; the projects target .NET Framework 4.6.2/4.7.2). CI's Windows MSI jobs are the first real build. - Manual QA of the reproduction from the incident is still to be done. - No existing test pins a 7.65 install, so the 7.65 → current upgrade on a domain controller may need a CI run to shake out. ### Additional Notes **Why the MSI and not `pkg/fleet/installer`** (per `.claude/rules/msi.md`): the affected path is specifically the manual MSI upgrade — fleet upgrades are unaffected. The bad credential is written by the WiX `ServiceInstall` element itself, and the fix must land between `InstallServices` and `StartDDServices` inside the same MSI transaction. `pkg/fleet/installer` is not in this code path. **Why disabling is safe:** every service uses `StartOn = null` / `StopOn = null`, `ConfigureServices` runs `When.After Step.InstallServices`, and `StartDDServices` runs later — so the service is disabled *before any logon attempt exists*. A disabled procmgr does not break the core Agent: `startDependentServices` only logs a warning when a dependent service fails to start. **Reverting is automatic.** `MajorUpgrade.Schedule = afterInstallInitialize` means every upgrade removes and recreates the services with `Start = demand`, so a disabled start type cannot persist. No registry flag or persistent state is needed. The has-password branch sets `Manual` explicitly anyway, so the outcome is deterministic rather than dependent on that sequencing. **Behavior change to be aware of:** while procmgr is disabled, DDOT / PAR / ADP do not run. Those hosts could not have run them anyway, since they need the same unavailable password. This is called out in the release note. **`ConfigureServiceUsers` went `private` → `internal`** so the tests can call it. `CustomActions/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` already declares `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("CustomActions.Tests")]` for exactly this, and `ConfigureUserCustomActions` already uses the same pattern. This does **not** widen the MSI's public surface. Testing through the public `ConfigureServices(Session)` is not viable: the test setup passes `rollbackDataName: null`, so the `finally { _rollbackDataStore.Store(); }` would NRE. **Rollback record deliberately omitted:** services are recreated on every upgrade, procmgr is created fresh in this transaction, and if an upgrade rolls back, leaving procmgr disabled is better than restoring a broken enabled-with-no-password config. **Not in this PR, follow-ups:** 1. **`ResetPeriodInDays = 0` is the actual reason a failed logon becomes a lockout.** It affects every dependent service. Setting it to `1` (or making the third action `none`) would bound any future crash-loop to 3 attempts. Small change, but it alters recovery behavior for all services, so it wants its own PR and QA. 2. Generic empty-password guard for all services, so the next new service can't repeat this. 3. Installer telemetry — the incident had no way to find other affected customers. 4. An `agent status` warning when procmgr is disabled for this reason. 5. #54735 / #54731 run procmgr as LocalSystem with spawn profiles, removing the ddagentuser logon entirely. Not backportable now; this MSI workaround can be relaxed once they land. Intended for backport to `7.82.x` for 7.82.3. Every production file touched is byte-identical between `main` and `origin/7.82.x`, so the cherry-pick should be conflict-free.

signals.title: fix(windows): don't fail uninstall when config directory or registry state is missing
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes the Windows `UninstallUser` MSI custom action so a missing registry install-state or config directory (`C:\ProgramData\Datadog` by default) no longer fails the whole uninstall. Splits `UninstallUser` into file-access and LSA-secret-removal steps so LSA cleanup always runs, guards against an unresolvable `DDAGENTUSER_NAME` operating on a bogus SID, and skips (rather than throws on) resetting base permissions when the config directory doesn't exist, while still resetting them when it does. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2107 If the registry key and/or config directory are removed out-of-band before uninstalling, the old code would throw uncaught when the directory was gone, failing the custom action entirely. ### Describe how you validated your changes `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall` already covers this: it deletes the registry key that persists `APPLICATIONDATADIRECTORY`, so uninstall falls back to the default `C:\ProgramData\Datadog`, which doesn't exist on that alt-dir install — reproducing the missing-directory failure this PR fixes.

signals.title: Fix ksm gvk collision
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a GroupVersionKind (GVK) collision in the Cluster Agent's kube-state-metrics (KSM) custom-resource collection. When two CRDs share the same `Kind` and plural name but belong to different API groups (e.g. `Project`/`projects` in both `artifactory.example.com` and `sonarqube.example.com`), they no longer collide onto a single API client. The KSM custom-resource client map was keyed by the bare plural name (`factory.Name()`, e.g. `"projects"`), which is group-blind. Two same-plural CRDs overwrote each other in the map, so both collectors' reflectors ended up sharing a single dynamic client bound to one group. The reflector for the other group then received objects of an unexpected GVK. Clients are now keyed by their fully-qualified GroupVersionResource on both the populate side (`discoverCustomResources` / `GetCustomResourceClientsAndCollectors`) and the lookup side (`getCustomResourceClient`), via a shared `CustomResourceClientKey` helper. This mirrors upstream KSM's own `CreateCustomResourceClients` keying. ### Motivation Customer escalation [CONS-8512](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONS-8512): a customer collecting custom-resource metrics for two `Project` CRDs in different API groups saw repeated `Unexpected watch event object gvk` errors in the Cluster Agent and incorrect, cross-contaminated project counts. Renaming a CRD is the only current workaround, which the customer cannot adopt. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Added unit tests in `pkg/kubestatemetrics/builder/gvk_collision_test.go`: - `CustomResourceClientKey` produces group-distinct keys for two same-plural CRDs. - Two same-plural/different-group resources each resolve their own client (no overwrite; each store's lookup, driven by its own `ExpectedType`, returns the matching client). - `bazel test //pkg/kubestatemetrics/builder:builder_test_dca` → PASSED. - `dda inv test` for `pkg/collector/corechecks/cluster/ksm/...` and `pkg/kubestatemetrics/builder/...` pass; `go vet` clean. ### Additional Notes - Agent-side only — no changes to the vendored/forked kube-state-metrics. - The populate and lookup sides both route through `util.GVRFromType(f.Name(), f.ExpectedType())`, so their keys are guaranteed to agree. Falls back to the plural name when a GVR cannot be derived, matching upstream KSM behavior. - Related upstream issue (separate manifestation in the standalone KSM binary): kubernetes/kube-state-metrics#2015. [CONS-8512]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONS-8512?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: feat(windows): enforce the config root security check on uninstall too
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Stacked on #55136. Extends that PR's config-root owner check to uninstall and upgrade-removal, which it currently skips, and trusts one more owner: - `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` now runs unconditionally in the MSI's `InstallExecuteSequence`, including on uninstall and removal for an upgrade, instead of being skipped there. It only asserts ownership and never changes anything, so it can't leave a partial uninstall behind. - `DDCreateFolders` now runs on every install/upgrade/repair/uninstall pass instead of only on first install, creating the config root if it's missing. It only resets an existing directory's permissions on a true first install, so upgrade/repair/uninstall never strips access (e.g. ddagentuser's) granted after the directory was first created. - The maintenance dialog's config-root check is now a single check on the Welcome dialog's `Next`, covering Change, Repair, and Remove alike, instead of a separate per-button check that skipped Remove. - `ContainerAdministrator` (the account Windows containers run as by default) is trusted alongside `Administrators`/`SYSTEM` in both the Go and MSI checks. ### Motivation Uninstall-time steps that depend on the config root (e.g. the fleet installer's `prerm` hook) should get the same defense-in-depth guarantee installation already has, instead of only install/upgrade/repair being covered. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New/updated `SecureDirectory` unit tests for the create-if-missing-without-reset behavior used outside first install, and for trusting `ContainerAdministrator`. - Fixed a race in `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall`: the test deleted the Agent's registry key while the service was still running, which could let the running Agent (as `ddagentuser`) recreate the default config directory itself before the fix stopped the service first.
signals.author: clarkb7

signals.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signals.text: Backport b8bc26ab93b6518c8688700c62fb1e6702d01efb from #55108. ___ ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors, by giving apt real per-request failover: - Rewrites the deb822 `URIs:` fields in `ubuntu.sources` to an ordered multi-URI list (`us-west-2`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `mirror.leaseweb.net`) so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - Drops `us-east-1` (the chronically-slow mirror in the timeout logs). - `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout so a slow mirror becomes a fast error that triggers failover. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs, across many branches). The build spent its whole wall-clock in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror. A first attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** fix it: apt's `mirror` method sticks to one mirror per invocation and only fails over when it's fully unreachable, so a slow-but-reachable `us-east-1` kept timing out and `Acquire::Retries` retried the same URI to the job timeout. This PR switches to explicit ordered `URIs:` for genuine per-request failover. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs isolated mirror throughput as the only variable (successful same-commit runs finished in 16-21m). - Validated the `sed` `URIs:` rewrite against the default noble `ubuntu.sources`. - CI will exercise the real build here. ### Additional Notes The same fix is applied to the other CI Dockerfiles in #55119. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: feat(windows): require the Agent configuration directory to be owned by an administrator
signals.text: _Re-lands #54269 (reverted for #incident-58787) unchanged. Follow-up fixes and the uninstall/upgrade-removal enforcement are stacked on top in #55133._ ### What does this PR do? Installation now fails when `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` already exists and is not owned by `Administrators` or `SYSTEM`, in both the MSI and the Go installer. The error names the owner found and the `takeown.exe` command to resolve it. - **MSI**: new `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` custom action after `InstallValidate`, so nothing has been changed on the system when it fails. It is skipped when uninstalling or being removed for an upgrade. The same check runs from the Welcome dialog and from maintenance Change/Repair, reporting through a popup; Remove is deliberately not checked. - **New `SecureDirectory` primitive** shared by `DDCreateFolders` and the rollback data store. It creates a directory with a protected SYSTEM/Administrators DACL, then reads the owner and applies permissions through a single handle that does not follow reparse points. - **Go installer**: `ensureDatadogDataDir` creates or validates the configuration directory, and `IsDirSecure` returns an actionable message. A new msiexec log pattern surfaces the failure in installer output. - **Error dialog**: replaces WixUI's `ErrorDlg` with `Custom_ErrorDialog`, sized like the existing modal, because the stock 205x60 text control clips these messages. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2998 Defense in depth. The Agent's configuration directory must be attributable to an administrator; if it already exists under another owner, resetting its permissions is not sufficient, so installation stops and explains how to resolve it instead of adopting the directory. This is a behavior change on both fresh installs and upgrades - existing installations are already compatible, since the MSI sets SYSTEM as the owner. Covered by the included `upgrade` release note. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New E2E test `TestInstallWithUntrustedConfigRoot`, wired into the `e2e_install_packages` job and run against AWS. - New tests for `SecureDirectory`, the MSI message escaping, `ensureDatadogDataDir`/`IsDirSecure`, and the msiexec log pattern - whose fixture is taken from a real MSI log. - Installed manually on a Windows VM with the configuration directory owned by a non-administrator, checking the message and the error dialog. - cross-ref'd ansible and chef packages to ensure compatability ### Additional Notes `Custom_ErrorDialog` is a renamed copy rather than a redefinition of `ErrorDlg`, since a WixUI library dialog cannot be redefined. Per the MSI spec it keeps `ErrorText` as its first control and all seven `Error*` buttons. MSI popup

signal.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded two independent ways: 1. **Flag allowlist** — the kernel only reports flags intersecting `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. `CLONE_NEWCGROUP` is excluded per the requester's note on CWS-6628 (it only moves the caller into the current cgroup namespace), as are the non-namespace flags. 2. **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of either gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. The `flags` field always carries the **full raw bitmask**, so rules can inspect any flag — including ones outside the allowlist — once an event fires. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: [CWS-6779] Implement the setns syscall
signal.text:
### What does this PR do? Adds a `setns` event to CWS: an eBPF hook on the `setns` syscall, a `setns` event in the event model wired through to SECL, a backend serializer, and functional test coverage. Fields exposed: | Field | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `setns.fd` | File descriptor of the namespace the thread requested to join | | `setns.nstype` | Requested namespace types — bitmask over the new `CLONE_NEW*` SECL constants (`0` = kernel infers the type from the fd) | | `setns.mntns` | MNTNS ID of the thread once the syscall returned | | `setns.netns` | NetNS ID of the thread once the syscall returned | | `setns.retval` | Return value (standard `SyscallEvent`) | Successful calls **and** `-EPERM`/`-EACCES` are reported (via the usual `IS_UNHANDLED_ERROR`), so denied attempts stay visible. ### Motivation CWS could already see namespace *creation* (`unshare_mntns`), but nothing fired when a thread *joined* an existing namespace. That is the primitive behind most container-escape and privilege-escalation chains: open `/proc/1/ns/net` (or any leaked nsfs fd), then `setns` into it. This gives the detection team signal to write rules against. A bare fd number is not rule-able on its own, so the event also resolves the namespace IDs the thread ends up in, which is what makes the escape detectable: ``` setns.nstype == CLONE_NEWNET && setns.netns == setns.mntns != ``` Those IDs come from extending `hook_switch_task_namespaces` — a hook that is already attached unconditionally and that `setns` necessarily goes through to commit its new `nsproxy`. Sequence: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as Thread (user space) participant K as Kernel participant E as eBPF (runtime-security) participant A as security-agent U->>K: setns(fd, nstype) K->>E: hook_setns — syscall entry E->>E: cache_syscall EVENT_SETNS {fd, nstype} K->>K: validate_nsset / commit_nsset K->>E: hook_switch_task_namespaces(task, new nsproxy) E->>E: read mnt_ns->inum / net_ns->inum
into the live EVENT_SETNS cache K->>E: hook_setns exit (or raw_syscalls:sys_exit tail call) E->>A: send_event EVENT_SETNS
{fd, nstype, mntns_id, netns_id, retval} A->>A: SECL evaluation over setns.* ``` Only mount and network are resolvable — `nsproxy_mnt_ns_offset` and `nsproxy_net_ns_offset` are the only `nsproxy` offsets available. Unresolved is reported as `0`. ### Describe how you validated your changes New `TestSetNS` (`pkg/security/tests/setns_test.go`) with four subtests, driven by a new `setns` command in `syscall_tester.c`. It is a C helper rather than Go on purpose: `setns` is per-thread, so calling it from the multi-threaded test binary would either fail (`CLONE_NEWNS` needs `fs->users == 1`) or strand a Go runtime thread in a foreign namespace. - `join-own-netns` / `join-own-mntns` — asserts `nstype`, `retval`, a valid `fd`, and that the reported ID equals the inode of `/proc/self/ns/{net,mnt}` - `infer-nstype` — `nstype == 0`; the requested type is reported as-is while the ID is still resolved - `netns-roundtrip` — holds a fd to the current netns, `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, then `setns` back. Asserts the reported netns is the **original** one and not the transient unshared one, which is what proves the ID is resolved per-event rather than read from a stale cache Each subtest also validates the serialized event against the new `setns.schema.json`. Run locally on a 6.x kernel (kprobe mode — this kernel forces the fentry fallback, so the fentry path is compile-verified here and covered functionally by KMT): | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `TestSetNS` | 4/4 pass | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/model` | 894 pass | | `bazel build //pkg/security/ebpf/...` | 20 targets; `sys_setns` + `handle_sys_setns_exit` present in both kprobe and fentry objects | | Regression check on namespace-adjacent tests | `TestPivotRoot`, `TestProcessContext`, `TestProcessSID`, `TestSetrlimitEvent`, `TestSocketEvent`, `TestBindEvent`, `TestConnectEvent*` all pass | | `golangci-lint` (`secl/model`, `serializers`, `probe`, `ebpf/probes`, `tests`) | 0 issues | | `validate-cws-generated-files` pre-push hook | Passed | Sample serialized event, captured from a live run: ```json "setns": { "fd": 3, "nstype": "CLONE_NEWNET", "mntns": 4026532592, "netns": 4026532595 } ``` ### Additional Notes **No release note**, intentionally — hence `changelog/no-changelog`. Worth a reviewer's opinion: this *is* user-facing (a new SECL event), so if you'd rather have it in the CHANGELOG, say so and I'll add a reno note and drop the label.
Design decisions worth a reviewer's eye - **`mntns`/`netns` are post-syscall values, not strictly "the namespace joined."** The kernel commits the whole `nsproxy`, so both are populated even for a `CLONE_NEWNET`-only call. The SECL docs are worded to say exactly that rather than overstate it. Filling both is strictly more informative than branching on the requested type — and for `nstype == 0` the type isn't known at entry anyway. - **`setns.fd` is `int`, not `int32`.** The accessor generator has no `setInt32FieldValue`, and no other exposed field uses `int32`. - **`nstype == 0` serializes as `"ANY"`.** The default bitmask stringer renders `""`, which reads as missing data; `0` is a documented, meaningful value for this syscall, so it got a name. - **eBPF only.** No ebpfless/ptracer wiring, matching how `setsid` and `pivot_root` shipped (`setrlimit` added ebpfless later in #44114). `TestSetNS` is deliberately absent from the ebpfless allowlist in `main_linux.go`, so it auto-skips there. - **No rate limiter.** `setns` is rare outside container runtimes and `nsenter`, unlike `setrlimit` which needed one. If QA on a busy node shows runtime chatter, a `pid_rate_limiter_allow` guard on the entry hook is the fix. - **Pre-existing wart, left alone:** `LastEventType` is still `PivotRootEventType` even though `setsid`/`nop`/`socket` come after it. It only bounds the `applyDefaultFilterPolicies` loop and mode `0` is `PolicyModeNoFilter`, so appending `setns` after it is harmless. Happy to fix separately.

signal.title: fix(system-probe): protect module loader registry with mutex during Register
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on the module loader registry: `Register` wrote `l.cfg`, `l.stats`, and iterated `l.modules` without holding the loader mutex, racing with `GetStats` which takes the lock. Added `l.Lock()` around the writes and snapshotted module entries before spawning stats goroutines. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes No unit test added — `Register` requires full eBPF factories, config, and dependencies that can't be constructed in a unit test, and duplicating the internal logic in a test wouldn't validate the actual fix. The race is eliminated by construction: all writes to the shared fields now go through the same mutex that `GetStats` already takes.

signal.title: [DO NOT MERGE] One-off e2e run with ADP enabled by default
signal.text: ## Summary Temporarily flips \`data_plane.enabled\` from \`false\` to \`true\` in the agent's compiled-in config default so that every e2e test in the full suite runs against ADP without requiring per-test changes or test duplication. The change is throwaway — close without merging once the CI run completes. This is the same config knob used by the AMP ADP test helpers (DADP-72, see [Slack thread](https://dd.slack.com/archives/C070PQKLLP5/p1783453441368899)). ## How to kick off the full e2e suite Trigger a new pipeline on this branch and set the CI variable: \`\`\` RUN_E2E_TESTS=on \`\`\` That variable hits the \`if_run_all_e2e_tests\` rule in \`.gitlab-ci.yml\` and flips all e2e jobs from manual to \`on_success\`. ## CI findings (ADP 1.5.1, branch jszwedko/run-ci-adp-enabled) ### Fixed in this PR - **Windows MSI \`status_command_infos\`**: All MSI test variants fail because \`agent_behaviour.go\` asserts the status output contains "DogStatsD". When ADP handles DSD, the \`DogStatsD\` status section is absent (the \`EnabledInternal()\` guard prevents registering the status provider). Fixed by accepting either "DogStatsD" or "Dogstatsd Metric Sample" (always present in the Aggregator section). ### Known pre-existing failures (ADP limitations, tracked in Saluki) - **\`TestReplayWithTagEnrichment\`** — ADP doesn't enrich replayed DSD packets with current tagger state. Tracked in Saluki. ### New failures requiring Saluki fixes - **Container DSD tests (ECS \`TestDogtstatsdUDP\`, \`TestDogtstatsdUDS\`; Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods)**: In container environments (ECS, K8s/Kind), fakeintake is configured as \`DD_ADDITIONAL_ENDPOINTS\` rather than \`dd_url\`. ADP doesn't appear to forward DogStatsD metrics to \`additional_endpoints\`, so no metrics arrive at fakeintake. In VM tests where fakeintake IS \`dd_url\` (primary endpoint), DSD forwarding works. This points to an \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding gap in ADP. - The Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods fail to become Ready — the workload pods mount \`/var/run/datadog/dsd.socket\` as a HostPath volume (type \`Socket\`). With ADP enabled, the core agent's DSD server doesn't start (so no socket is created); ADP must create it but apparently doesn't complete socket setup in time or at the expected path. - Root cause: ADP \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding — active Saluki config migration work (issues #2312–#2316) may be the upstream cause. ### Other failures under investigation - **Anomaly detection tests** — under investigation, may be ADP-independent - **GPU tests** — under investigation ## Test plan - No new tests. The goal is to observe which existing e2e tests break when ADP is the default. - \`new-e2e-amp-adp\` (existing) runs the AMP suite filtered to \`--run "ADP"\` tests; this PR covers the rest. **DO NOT MERGE** — this default flip must not land on \`main\`.

signal.title: fix(windows): don't fail uninstall when config directory or registry state is missing
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes the Windows `UninstallUser` MSI custom action so a missing registry install-state or config directory (`C:\ProgramData\Datadog` by default) no longer fails the whole uninstall. Splits `UninstallUser` into file-access and LSA-secret-removal steps so LSA cleanup always runs, guards against an unresolvable `DDAGENTUSER_NAME` operating on a bogus SID, and skips (rather than throws on) resetting base permissions when the config directory doesn't exist, while still resetting them when it does. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2107 If the registry key and/or config directory are removed out-of-band before uninstalling, the old code would throw uncaught when the directory was gone, failing the custom action entirely. ### Describe how you validated your changes `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall` already covers this: it deletes the registry key that persists `APPLICATIONDATADIRECTORY`, so uninstall falls back to the default `C:\ProgramData\Datadog`, which doesn't exist on that alt-dir install — reproducing the missing-directory failure this PR fixes.
signal.author: clarkb7

signal.title: feat(windows): enforce the config root security check on uninstall too
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Stacked on #55136. Extends that PR's config-root owner check to uninstall and upgrade-removal, which it currently skips, and trusts one more owner: - `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` now runs unconditionally in the MSI's `InstallExecuteSequence`, including on uninstall and removal for an upgrade, instead of being skipped there. It only asserts ownership and never changes anything, so it can't leave a partial uninstall behind. - `DDCreateFolders` now runs on every install/upgrade/repair/uninstall pass instead of only on first install, creating the config root if it's missing. It only resets an existing directory's permissions on a true first install, so upgrade/repair/uninstall never strips access (e.g. ddagentuser's) granted after the directory was first created. - The maintenance dialog's config-root check is now a single check on the Welcome dialog's `Next`, covering Change, Repair, and Remove alike, instead of a separate per-button check that skipped Remove. - `ContainerAdministrator` (the account Windows containers run as by default) is trusted alongside `Administrators`/`SYSTEM` in both the Go and MSI checks. ### Motivation Uninstall-time steps that depend on the config root (e.g. the fleet installer's `prerm` hook) should get the same defense-in-depth guarantee installation already has, instead of only install/upgrade/repair being covered. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New/updated `SecureDirectory` unit tests for the create-if-missing-without-reset behavior used outside first install, and for trusting `ContainerAdministrator`. - Fixed a race in `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall`: the test deleted the Agent's registry key while the service was still running, which could let the running Agent (as `ddagentuser`) recreate the default config directory itself before the fix stopped the service first.

signal.title: feat(windows): require the Agent configuration directory to be owned by an administrator
signal.text: _Re-lands #54269 (reverted for #incident-58787) unchanged. Follow-up fixes and the uninstall/upgrade-removal enforcement are stacked on top in #55133._ ### What does this PR do? Installation now fails when `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` already exists and is not owned by `Administrators` or `SYSTEM`, in both the MSI and the Go installer. The error names the owner found and the `takeown.exe` command to resolve it. - **MSI**: new `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` custom action after `InstallValidate`, so nothing has been changed on the system when it fails. It is skipped when uninstalling or being removed for an upgrade. The same check runs from the Welcome dialog and from maintenance Change/Repair, reporting through a popup; Remove is deliberately not checked. - **New `SecureDirectory` primitive** shared by `DDCreateFolders` and the rollback data store. It creates a directory with a protected SYSTEM/Administrators DACL, then reads the owner and applies permissions through a single handle that does not follow reparse points. - **Go installer**: `ensureDatadogDataDir` creates or validates the configuration directory, and `IsDirSecure` returns an actionable message. A new msiexec log pattern surfaces the failure in installer output. - **Error dialog**: replaces WixUI's `ErrorDlg` with `Custom_ErrorDialog`, sized like the existing modal, because the stock 205x60 text control clips these messages. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2998 Defense in depth. The Agent's configuration directory must be attributable to an administrator; if it already exists under another owner, resetting its permissions is not sufficient, so installation stops and explains how to resolve it instead of adopting the directory. This is a behavior change on both fresh installs and upgrades - existing installations are already compatible, since the MSI sets SYSTEM as the owner. Covered by the included `upgrade` release note. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New E2E test `TestInstallWithUntrustedConfigRoot`, wired into the `e2e_install_packages` job and run against AWS. - New tests for `SecureDirectory`, the MSI message escaping, `ensureDatadogDataDir`/`IsDirSecure`, and the msiexec log pattern - whose fixture is taken from a real MSI log. - Installed manually on a Windows VM with the configuration directory owned by a non-administrator, checking the message and the error dialog. - cross-ref'd ansible and chef packages to ensure compatability ### Additional Notes `Custom_ErrorDialog` is a renamed copy rather than a redefinition of `ErrorDlg`, since a WixUI library dialog cannot be redefined. signal.title: fix(installer): secure Windows config rollback
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes Windows Fleet Automation config experiment rollback so it: - copies YAML ACLs from a securely created backup directory - removes only allowlisted Fleet-managed YAML that is absent from the backup - preserves unmanaged files and directories under `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` - rejects incomplete YAML copies and legacy symlink mismatches before deleting the backup - uses slash-aware allowlist matching and root-confined deletion to avoid over-deleting YAML or following swapped junctions - reconciles legacy v2 managed symlinks (`stable` / `experiment`) before robocopy and verifies they are restored Adds selective-cleanup, copy-validation, legacy-link, and Windows ACL/unmanaged-file regression tests, plus a release note. ### Motivation Addresses [WINA-2053](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2053) and the failure observed in [SPFA-180](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SPFA-180). The current `robocopy /MIR /SL ... *.yaml` rollback can purge destination content and recreates deleted files without their original ACLs. Adding `/SEC` by itself was previously unsafe because an unprivileged user could pre-create the destination between deletion and ACL repair while retaining an open handle. The current implementation now securely creates the experiment root with the stable root's security descriptor before copying, and never removes the stable root before restore. This change uses that prerequisite, removes `/MIR`, scopes rollback deletion in Go to managed YAML only, and treats robocopy mismatch exit codes 4-7 as rollback failure. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/config --no-cache` (64 passed) - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/fleet/installer/config --only-modified-packages` - `bazelisk test //pkg/fleet/installer/config:config_test` - `bazelisk build //pkg/fleet/installer/config:config --platforms=@rules_go//go/toolchain:windows_amd64` - Pre-commit and pre-push hooks, including release-note validation Windows-only tests cover ACL restore, junction rejection, and v2 symlink rollback, including backups whose copied absolute `stable`/`experiment` links still point at the original tree (`robocopy /SL`). Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) [WINA-2053]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2053?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [SPFA-180]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SPFA-180?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: fix(logonduration): make the boot_timeline offset axis monotone
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the `boot_timeline` axis monotone, so a milestone can no longer render ahead of one that happened before it. `bootOffsetFunc` collapsed the login-screen wait in a **single step**: `ts >= SessionLogon` was pulled left by the whole `SessionLogon - LoginUIDone` gap, everything else kept its raw offset. A step function is not order-preserving, and since the collapse maps `SessionLogon` onto `LoginUIDone`'s raw offset, the payload carried two clocks on one origin — an in-gap milestone at *how deep into the wait it started*, a post-logon one at *how long after logon it happened*. Nothing forces the first to be smaller. On the Aug 17 boot `computer_group_policy` lands at 10807 while `user_group_policy`, 25.7 s later in wall clock, lands at 8839. The premise the collapse rests on is false: that window is not idle. Machine Group Policy runs in it on all four traces we have, real and synthetic. **Fix:** elide only the sub-intervals of `[LoginUIDone, SessionLogon)` that no observed milestone covers. `offset(ts) = (ts - BootStart) - (elided time elapsed by ts)`. The derivative is 1 outside those stretches and 0 inside, so it is monotone by construction, and no milestone span can be elided because elision only happens where nothing was observed and a span *is* an observation. Nothing is truncated — an interval running past `SessionLogon` has no idle behind it to remove, so the overlap survives. It degrades to today's numbers when the region really is empty, and the timeline lengthens by exactly the busy time previously erased: +3483 ms on Aug 17, +49 ms on Aug 4, each the machine pass duration. The milestone candidate list moves into `timelineCandidates`, consumed by both the renderer and the busy-interval builder, so a milestone can never be rendered from an interval the axis did not know about. `group_policy_details` is fixed by the same change with no edit to `grouppolicy.go` — `finalize` already calls `bootOffsetFunc` for every CSE offset, so the child inversion clears with the parent. `durations` and `total_boot_duration_ms` are raw pairwise measurements and do not move. ### Motivation `boot_timeline` is a rendering axis; consumers read left-to-right as chronological. On a domain-joined machine it silently violated that on most boots, and `group_policy_details` now hangs off those milestones, so a wrong parent offset drags a child tree with it. The defect arrived with #50027 (`9b2dab34afc`), which introduced the login-screen gap collapse. It has never had a WINA ticket — worth filing before merge, since this moves a shipped number. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logonduration/impl` — **160 passing, 0 failing**. `dda inv linter.go` — 0 issues. The primary guard is a property test, `TestBootTimelineOffsetsAreMonotone`: sorted by wall-clock `Timestamp`, `OffsetMs` must be non-decreasing. Stronger than fixed expectations, holds for any input, and **fails on the shipped code** against the exact numbers the old test asserted. Runs over `fullBootTimeline` and all four new fixtures. `TestCSEOffsetsShareTheBootTimelineAxis` passes **unmodified** — its region has no busy interval, so it is elided whole. That it still passes is the evidence the change is confined to in-region activity. Four new cases in `TestBuildTimelineMilestones`, plus updated "full timeline" offsets (elided 2000 + 9000, not the full 19000): - **pass straddles `SessionLogon`** — the case that proves nothing is truncated: `8746..37275` against `logon_duration` at `34424..45097`, overlapping by exactly the 2851 ms the pass ran past logon - **pass absent** — full region elided, offsets identical to today - **`MachineGPEnd` absent** — pass has no span, region elided whole, point clamps to region start - **pass reaching in from before `LoginUIDone`** — only the idle after it is elided, bar keeps its full width New `TestCSEOffsetsKeepPassesInOrderAcrossTheLoginScreen` covers the reported shape the existing suite misses: a computer pass *inside* the region with CSEs alongside a user pass after logon, asserting each invocation nests in its parent and that the whole computer scope precedes the user scope. One expectation changed outside the plan: `TestCollector_FullBootSequence` asserted a CSE at 14000; it starts at boot+14s with 2000 ms elided ahead of it, so it is now 12000, still nested in its parent at `10000..18000`. **Not done:** the analyzer has not been re-run over the WINA-2940 boot ETL against this diff. The Aug 4 / Aug 17 figures come from the investigation that produced the change, not from executing this code on a capture. ### Additional Notes **`impl_darwin.go` is deliberately left on the single-step pattern.** The fix is a provable no-op there — its only candidates are `boot_duration`, `login_window_ready` (a point at the region start) and `logon_duration`, so nothing can land inside the region and it is elided whole either way. **CSE invocations are deliberately not in the busy list.** They live inside their pass, so they add nothing while it is present, and wiring `gpAccumulator` into the offset function would invert the current dependency. Follow-up for the case where an 8000 is missing and the pass has no span but its CSEs do. **Limit:** the rule does not establish the region is idle, only that nothing was observed there. Uninstrumented machine work at the login screen is still elided as think-time — that assumption is the feature's, unchanged since #50027. What this removes is the assumption erasing intervals we *did* observe. Left for their own PRs: `LoginUIDone` pair selection, `boot_timeline` array ordering (emitted in candidate order, never sorted — now a one-line change with no correctness question attached), unpaired pass endpoints, and WINA-3011 truncation. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  ci(ddot): make otel apt mirror resilient to slow mirrors
signal.text: Backport b8bc26ab93b6518c8688700c62fb1e6702d01efb from #55108. ___ ### What does this PR do? Makes the apt package-mirror config in `Dockerfiles/agent-ddot/Dockerfile.agent-otel` (used by `docker_image_build_otel`) resilient to *slow* mirrors, by giving apt real per-request failover: - Rewrites the deb822 `URIs:` fields in `ubuntu.sources` to an ordered multi-URI list (`us-west-2`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `mirror.leaseweb.net`) so apt fails over to the next mirror on error. - Drops `us-east-1` (the chronically-slow mirror in the timeout logs). - `Acquire::Retries "1"` + 10s timeout so a slow mirror becomes a fast error that triggers failover. ### Motivation `docker_image_build_otel` intermittently timed out (~3% of runs, across many branches). The build spent its whole wall-clock in `apt-get install build-essential` against a congested `us-east-1` mirror. A first attempt (mirror+file peer list + Acquire timeout) did **not** fix it: apt's `mirror` method sticks to one mirror per invocation and only fails over when it's fully unreachable, so a slow-but-reachable `us-east-1` kept timing out and `Acquire::Retries` retried the same URI to the job timeout. This PR switches to explicit ordered `URIs:` for genuine per-request failover. ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI Visibility + job logs isolated mirror throughput as the only variable (successful same-commit runs finished in 16-21m). - Validated the `sed` `URIs:` rewrite against the default noble `ubuntu.sources`. - CI will exercise the real build here. ### Additional Notes The same fix is applied to the other CI Dockerfiles in #55119. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
